name: The reprobate mind
about: Men given over by God after they reject Him: Romans 1, hardened hearts, and knowing them by their fruits.

teachings.title: Reprobates are children of the devil
teachings.summary: From Titus 1:16 and Acts 13:10 he teaches that reprobates, who profess God but deny Him in works, are the children of the devil working all unrighteousness.
teachings.text:
**Titus 1:16**
*They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Reprobates are the children of the devil, who work all unrighteousness.

**Acts 13:10**
*And said, O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?*

teachings.title: Jude: trees without fruit, twice dead
teachings.summary: Jude warns saved believers to keep reprobate, ungodly men out of the churches while still winning souls with compassion and with fear.
teachings.text:
We see in Jude an epistle to saved Christians, to whom the Gospel had already been delivered, warning them of those others who are reprobate in the faith, trees without fruit, twice-dead, plucked up...

There's reason this parallel book to 2 Peter, reiterating many of the same themes and warnings, and echoing Romans 1, is included right before Revelation.

It is both a warning to keep these abominations out of the various local churches and to win souls to Christ, saving who they can with charity and if need be, fear, warning them of the fire that awaits those unrighteous and ungodly men who tempt the unsaved away from the true Gospel.

teachings.title: Having a form of godliness
teachings.summary: 2 Timothy 3 lists the marks of the reprobate, false teachers ever learning yet never coming to the truth, and believers should flee them and rely on scripture alone.
teachings.text:
This final instalment of a study on Reprobate Doctrine contains yet another list of their attributes by Paul (Romans 1:18-32 is another).

We see the nature of our enemy, and how they will grow worse and worse as time goes by.

Many false teachers seek to subvert the doctrine as they themselves are examples of it, *having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof*.

"*Ever learning but never coming to the knowledge of the* truth" reminds me of the Ortho Gnome creature I posted about this morning. They will pridefully tell you all the books and "church fathers" they've read that reinforce their error, while mocking those who rely on the Bible alone for doctrine. From these, flee, because we know "*All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness*."

teachings.title: Agrippa's mockery and the reprobate mind
teachings.summary: Agrippa's mocking response to Paul marks him as reprobate, since the reprobate mind knows the truth of salvation yet rejects it with a hardened heart and seared conscience.
teachings.text:
Festus yelling out, "*Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad*" is a familiar tactic of those proud in their own conceits when confronted with the truth of the word. We see this mockery and derision often, when we speak out for the Lord. Especially when it's done confidently and with knowledge of the scriptures. Left with having to either acknowledge the truth or save face and defend the status they hold in pride, most choose to be scornful.

And Agrippa, who history paints as a hedonist, possibly engaged in incest with his sister Bernice (who is present for this), laughingly says Paul has almost convinced him to be a Christian.

I believe him to be reprobate, based on this mocking response. One quality of the reprobate mind according to Romans 1, is that *knowing the truth*, they reject it. I find this true in my own experience with them. Most reprobates when pushed understand the basics of salvation and Christ. Often better than some who call themselves Christian but who are caught up in damnable heresy. It's a head knowledge coupled with a hardness of heart and stiffness of neck, that brought them to be twice-dead, conscience seared.

Paul expresses the fervent hope that all who hear him come to saving faith, that the hearers be as he is, absent his current bonds, and with that they dismiss him. Agrippa then says that while Paul hasn't done anything to be held, his appeal unto Caesar has sealed his fate. Paul is destined for Rome.

teachings.title: Examine yourselves whether ye be reprobate
teachings.summary: In 2 Corinthians 13 Paul turns the Corinthians' accusations back on them, asking whether they themselves are reprobate, which shows that Christians may judge the signs of reprobation such as sodomy and false gospels by what people say and do.
teachings.text:
Final chapter, Paul finishes his rebuke of the Corinthian church in stinging fashion.

He says he's coming back, and in the manner established in God's law and Christ's teaching on church discipline, before 2 or 3 witnesses Paul will establish who is telling the truth, and who exactly it is that needs credentials to be established. That if he has to come there again it will not be to spare those who seek proof of his having Christ in him.

He says examine your own selves, if they have Christ within them. If they think Paul doesn't, and that Christ is within them so mightily, sarcastically accusing them of not being saved. Of perhaps being reprobate.

This seems harsh. We hear all the time that we shouldn't "reprobate someone." Even when the person is exhibiting the signs of reprobation, sodomy, being a false prophet with a damnable false gospel, many Christians today will say we cannot judge what is in another's heart. But we can judge what they say and do, if not the reason. The Corinthians who disputed Paul's salvation were passively accusing him of being a reprobate. Of preaching a false gospel. Of being a grifter.

And so Paul opens both barrels and questions if they are still in the sins he'd written to them about before, if perhaps they themselves are reprobate.

Paul does take pains to make room for the sincere believers within that church.

And he says, he'd hope that even if he and his associates were reprobate, they'd still comport themselves without sin, doing evil. It's hard preaching, because it puts those balking at giving alms and using the railing accusations against the Apostle to do it, on the hook that regardless of others, they should live as befits saints, (knowing they do not).

He concludes the rebuke with a threat of coming with the sharpness of the gifts he has through the Holy Ghost, but assuring it would be to their edification, not destruction. Again it's a sarcastic dig at the problems in the church while assuring the brethren.

He finishes with a flourish of kindness and grace, and salutations in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Amen.

teachings.title: Unto every good work reprobate
teachings.summary: Titus 1:16 describes Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican clergy, works-based false salvationists, LDS and JW leaders and Calvinist lordshippers, who are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness and whose mouths must be stopped by the word of God.
teachings.text:
*Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled. They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Every ordained Catholic priest, cardinal and 'pope.' Every Orthodox monk and Anglican bishop. Every works-based false salvationist. Every cult leader of LDS or JW. Calvinist lordshiper 'reformed' viper, with their corrupt modern translations. All of them.

They are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness. And over and over again scripture teaches us to be Biblical Fundamentalists, to cling to God's word, and to reject those who seek to turn others from the truth. Others who, with itching ears and mired in their own sins, can be turned from the truth by these vain talkers. Their mouths must be stopped, and it is by the word of God that we shut them up.

teachings.title: Judge doctrine, not another's walk
teachings.summary: We should not judge a person's standing with God by his works or sins, but we can judge by his doctrine, and one trusting in anything but the gospel can be counted unsaved.
teachings.text:
A common argument made by heretics who haven't taken correction after one or two admonishments with scripture is that "only God can judge if I am wrong."

And while that's true, we are blessed to know His judgment as God has laid out precisely what the correct doctrine of salvation is in a way that's clear and understandable.

Don't assume one's relationship with God by their works or sins. It's hypocritical and you don't know the full story, nor can you know where the Spirit may lead them.

But you can absolutely judge by their doctrine. And if they tell you they don't believe the Gospel and are trusting in something other than it to be justified, you can safely consider them unsaved.

teachings.title: Children of the devil are spiritual seed
teachings.summary: He rejects the serpent seed doctrine as damnable and teaches that the children of the devil are reprobates given over by God, a spiritual seed that does not reproduce but recruits.
teachings.text:
It should not have to be said that the perverted and disgusting false doctrine that Eve had relations with the serpent is from the pitts of Hell and those damned reprobates who promote it are to be rejected, utterly.

Yes, there are children of the devil. They are those who are reprobate, given up and given over by God. They are of their father, the devil. Sons of Belial. That synagogue of Satan. It isn't a physical seed, but a spiritual one, and they don't reproduce, the recruit though guile, trauma, abuse, and appeals to the flesh. And they seek to do his will, and are at enmity with God and with humanity. Murderers from the first.

teachings.title: The way of Cain, the first reprobate
teachings.summary: Jude warns against reprobates who teach the damnable heresy of works and turn liberty into lasciviousness, using Cain as the first reprobate and first works-based heretic.
teachings.text:
In the epistle of Jude, he writes of the common salvation, *that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.*

*For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ....Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain...*

The way of Cain is the way of works, self-righteousness, wrath, giving way to sin, and stubbornness and stiff-necked willful refusal to accept the gift of common salvation, *denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.*

Jude is warning against reprobates, who teach damnable heresy of works, and turning liberty into lasciviousness, using Cain as an example, the first reprobate. The first works-based heretic.

teachings.title: Reprobates and the nature of evil
teachings.summary: He says many reject the reprobate doctrine because they do not understand evil, which often looks pitiable rather than malevolent, while reprobate false teachers use mercy to take advantage, as Jesus understood in Matthew 23.
teachings.text:
I think some of the hangups people have with accepting the reprobate Doctrine is an inability to understand evil. That evil, often isn't an outward appearance of malevolence like a comic book super villain. It's often someone who is a miserable human being. Who are sad and pathetic creatures. We take pity on them often, and they use our good-natured inclination for mercy and Grace to take advantage of us. In ways Great and Small. They are the false teachers, the false prophets bringing doctrines of damnation. Who have the appearance of holiness, so much so that they could fool the very elect if possible. Whited sepulchers full of death and bones, decaying flesh. I posted it a few days ago, but the final sermon Jesus gives in Matthew 23 is addressed directly to the reprobates before him. Vipers and hypocrites, Jesus calls them, and says they can't escape the damnation of hell.

Jesus understood the nature of them. It's a shame most humans fail to grasp it.

teachings.title: Thorns and briers rejected and burned
teachings.summary: Hebrews 6:8's thorns and briers are the same as the corrupt trees, tares and fruitless trees of Matthew 7 and Jude, namely the reprobates turned over by God whose end is to be burned.
teachings.text:
*For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

They that bear thorns and briers. Thistles. Corrupt fruit.

**Matthew 7:15-20**
*Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.*

As it is written in Jude; *clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots.*

It's the same allusion, and one repeated throughout scripture. They are the tares. As we see in verses 8 of Hebrews chapter 6; *But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

These are the reprobates. Turned over to a reprobate mind by God, rejected. Their end is to be burned.

teachings.title: Wisdom is justified of all her children
teachings.summary: Jesus likened the Pharisees to petulant children at play, and their worldly wisdom was shown by its fruit, people unable to come to the truth.
teachings.text:
Finishing up Luke chapter 7, Jesus had just dealt with the doubting of John the Baptist by proxy, the disciples of John sent away having seen the signs and wonders of Jesus, after asking for confirmation that He was who John, sitting in prison, believed. Having heard rumors and gossip, and tales of extraordinary miracles, even the raising of the dead, John's faith had been tested. Was it too good to be true?

And Jesus gives a sermon to those there to reaffirm that John was the greatest prophet born of men. Not a reed bent by the wind. Not as the Pharisees and Sadducees, decked in fine and comfortable clothes. He came to the wilderness wearing sackcloth and preaching repentance unto salvation, by faith in the coming Christ.

And by this, even more sinners believed and we're baptized, justifying God.

But the Pharisees didn't believe and rejected the counsel of God.

And so Jesus, preaching to the crowd but referring to the "holy men," asks rhetorically, what can He compare them to?

He says they are like children at play. Kids playing a game, where they pretend to be at a feast, or playact a funeral march, and who are angry when prophets like John or Jesus do not act in the manner they think they should. "*We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.*"

It's a deeply insulting comparison. Jesus is pointing out their childishness. Their spiritual immaturity and petulance. That they expect the prophets of God to play the same game of hypocrisy and pretend that they call holy and righteous, with flowing robes of comfortable and rich clothing, sitting in sanctimonious judgment of others, while, as Jesus says elsewhere, they are actually vipers. Frauds. Playacting.

*But wisdom is justified of all her children.*

That is, again using justified in the same manner as earlier in the chapter, it is evidenced. Validated. The children of wisdom here is the fruit of the judgment of these men. Their earthly wisdom is seen by the fruit it has produced. Jesus is saying basically, you've rejected the counsel of God, had poor judgment of John, and now of me, and your wisdom, or lack thereof, is evidenced by the children it has produced. People unable to come to the knowledge of the truth, and who will be gathered and burned like chaff.

teachings.title: The reprobate Jews as whited sepulchres
teachings.summary: Jesus' late preaching in Luke 13 and Matthew 23 was aimed at the reprobate Jewish leaders, hypocrites relying on genealogy and works who are the tares and fruitless trees, unable to come to repentance.
teachings.text:
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness. Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.*

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.*

*Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of Hell?*

*Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.*

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

*Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.*

It is important to point out that in chapter 13 of Luke, which I covered somewhat this morning, much of the preaching done by Jesus, if not all of it, was not to disciples, to the saved, though many may have been present and there is application for us today as believers. It was to non-believers and, especially as His ministry wound down to His eventual crucifixion, He is preaching harder and harder against the reprobate Jews. The holy men, so called, hypocrites and vipers. And those they've made twice the child of Hell as themselves.

They are the fowls of the air, perching on the mustard tree that is the Kingdom of Heaven. They are the leaven hidden in the meal that spreads throughout. They are those who seek to enter by the wide gate of their works and self-righteousness. They are those without the white raiment given the guests of the wedding who came when bidden, crashing the wedding.

They are those saying "Lord, Lord, look upon my works." The virgins without oil in their lamps. The servant who didn't think the Lord would come, and instead ate, drank and was merry. They are the man counted among the share of the unbelieving. The man, given much who received the worse stripes.

They, knowing the judgment of God reject it. They put off getting right with God, obeying the Gospel, thinking that when brought before the magistrate they will be able to plea their case.

They are those who rather than striving towards the strait gate, contending for the faith, that they may be saved to do the work of the Lord, count on their genealogies and self-righteous works and adhering to the letter of the law, the ordinances and customs, but inside are whited sepulchers. Full of dead men's bones. Faithless and hopeless. Tares among the wheat, fit to be gathered and burned. The tree without fruit. Unable to come to repentance. Reprobate silver.

teachings.title: Tares among the wheat
teachings.summary: A professed ex-sodomite who claims salvation by repenting of sin is a red flag, since Jesus, Peter and Jude all teach that reprobates creep into churches as tares among the wheat and can be known by their traits.
teachings.text:
"But this guy came to our church saying he was a sodomite for years and repented of it so he's saved!"

Repentance of sin isn't how we are saved. It is by faith alone. Right away it is a red flag, or should be.

**Matthew 13:24-30**
*Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way. But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares? He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up? But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.*

The tares, or weeds that resemble wheat but produce no fruit, Jesus warned they would be sown among believers.

Peter writes of reprobates coming in to churches, **2 Peter 2**, he preaches hard against them, calling them *natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption; and shall receive the reward of unrighteousness.*

These are the tares among the wheat. This is the reprobate doctrine, and the warning that they shall creep in unawares, and sow discord and lead many astray.

**2 Peter 2:17-22**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.*

Peter is teaching the same Reprobate Doctrine as Paul.

And Jude;

*Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not. And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities...*

Jude also provides a list of traits that you might know them, similar to Paul's in **Romans 1**:

teachings.title: Filled with all unrighteousness
teachings.summary: He teaches that those given over to a reprobate mind are given up to vile affections and over time filled with all the sins of Romans 1:29-31, the traits of psychopaths, and that all sodomites are reprobate though not all reprobates are sodomites.
teachings.text:
*And for this cause* *God gave them up*...

It is rejecting God, His judgment, the conviction of the Spirit, our conscience which is the law of God written in our hearts. The revelation of God's wrath upon sin. They reject all of it.

*And for this cause God gave them up...*

They do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. They turn the truth of God into a lie. They worship the created more than the Creator, who is blessed forever, amen.

*And for this cause God gave them up...*

And God gives them up to what? Vile affections. To do those things which are not convenient, that is proper and natural. Working that which is unseemly. And so receive in themselves that recompense of their error which was meet. They get to experience the misery of getting what they want, being utterly rejected by the God who they did not want to know.

And sodomy is a consequence of being given over to a reprobate mind.

But more, they are *filled* with all unrighteousness. Over time and as their twice-dead, conscience seared condition grows, as they become more the child of the devil with each passing day, knowing Hell awaits them, that what they do is deserving death (they know, verse 32 makes it clear), they are filled up with unrighteousness.

*Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful*...

These qualities are found in all reprobates. And many are sins common to man, anyway. We all experience envy, but aren't filled with it. Many commit fornication, many are proud, we boast, we disobey our parents. But we aren't filled with all of it. You will notice the more you understand this doctrine, just how true all of this list is in regards to these dogs. Especially the implacable and unmerciful trait that they have. They are impossible to please and they seek vengeance and destruction of others, with maliciousness. They hate God. They gossip and betray others. They invent new ways of evil. They have no natural affection.

These traits mirror what science of men call psychopaths. They are the malignant narcissists and blank-stare killers, pedophiles and rapists without mercy. Not all reprobates are sodomites, but all sodomites are reprobate.

teachings.title: Preaching the reprobate doctrine against wolves
teachings.summary: He teaches that reprobates are children of Belial by free will choice, capable of evil a normal mind cannot imagine, and that the reprobate doctrine must be preached so believers do not let them into homes and churches.
teachings.text:
And so, we understand and recognize the process. How the children of man are unregenerate sinners, and children of God those saved by faith. And children of Belial, those whose father is the Devil, as Jesus said, are those given up, given over to a reprobate mind. Rejected of God.

*Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron*, as Paul wrote to Timothy.

We can see that this is a free will choice, just as salvation is. We can see the process unfold throughout scripture.

We gain understanding of their nature and what evil they are capable of. And the Bible stresses these things because the inventions of evil that these ravenous wolves come up with cannot be imagined by a normal mind.

We cannot truly understand their depravity and wickedness, because they are not things the natural man can comprehend, saved or unsaved.

It is this innocence that they prey upon to come in and corrupt the faithful. We empathize and we compromise because we can't imagine that level of wickedness, or we are carried away by our own sin. Pride especially.

And not knowing scripture, and not accepting the judgment of God that those who do such things are worthy of death, people open up their homes and churches to these filthy dreamers.

And so we preach the Reprobate Doctrine, that all may be throughly furnished to stand against them. Especially in this month of "pride" where the haters of God promote their wickedness as good, proudly, and call Godliness evil.

teachings.title: Mark them which cause divisions
teachings.summary: God has marked reprobates in two clear ways, being sodomites or false teachers who usurp the Gospel for gain and lead others astray, and believers are commanded to mark and avoid them rather than dismiss these warnings.
teachings.text:
The eternal salute of these saints in Christ, who Paul calls fellow laborers in the preserved word of God is a mighty honor. Their qualities of faith and work towards the ministry of the Gospel are an example we should strive for.

Paul, having called out those he sought to honor to the churches in Rome, can't help but add more doctrine to what has been a master class of Christian theology.

Mark them which cause divisions. Who are teaching contrary to the doctrines they have learned. We have learned the same, being blessed by scripture. Then this command is for us as well. We should mark them and avoid them.

*For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.*

A major theme to the epistles is warning against false prophets and those bringing in damnable heresy, and what is consistently noted is their tendency to be in it for filthy lucre sake. As Jesus said in **Matthew 23**;

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.*

Or Paul writing in **2 Timothy 3**;

*For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts, Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.*

False teachers are vipers. Reprobates. Dogs. Swine. **Never** able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Starting with warnings about reprobates, Paul finishes on the same topic from a different angle, and understanding that God has marked the reprobate in two distinct and clear ways that man may know who they are; if they are sodomites or false teachers (often both) who usurp the authority of the Gospel to promote damnable heresy and lead others astray, they are all together corrupt.

This isn't someone who is wrong on some secondary or tertiary doctrine. Or someone who disagrees with you about some verse meaning or whatever. It isn't an unsaved person who doesn't understand the Gospel.

This is the curse of those who turn the truth of God into a lie. Who hold the truth in unrighteousness. Who knowingly subvert and undermine churches for their own pleasure, recognition or wealth, passing themselves off as men of God.

**Jude 10-13**
*But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.*

Some people think that many who preach the Reprobate Doctrine spend too much time on it, or consider it wrong to make assumptions about people's status as a saved Christian, or not. And generally speaking, we should give a professing brother or sister the benefit of the doubt. Carefully and with love correcting them from scripture if they stray. If it is a minor thing, like in Romans 14, we should ignore it and humor them in it that we not lead them to sin.

Given that context, and the understanding that, despite that understanding, the holy Spirit has inspired verse after verse, chapter after chapter, from multiple writers, over and over again in the New Testament, giving these warnings and how to recognize them. It is clearly for our edification. Those that reject it do so at their peril.

teachings.title: Examine yourselves, except ye be reprobates
teachings.summary: From 2 Corinthians 13 he teaches that who is of God and who is reprobate is established by the works done, so false teachers are judged by their fruit.
teachings.text:
As for Paul, there are Corinthians justifying grave sin by saying the Apostle isn't qualified to rebuke them.

He levels exactly his credentials;

*Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you. For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God*...
*Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?*

He cities the work of salvation in them by his own testimony of the gospel towards them. If he isn't qualified to rebuke them, then how were they begotten of Christ through him? Are they reprobates?

And if they have Christ in them due to Paul's preaching, could he be a reprobate?

Here is wisdom; that we can establish who is of God and who isn't by the works done.

False teachers are judged by their fruit.

They don't produce thousands of salvations, ordained pastors, multiple churches planted, if they are not of God. Paul certainly shut up those protesting his qualifications by reminding them of this simple fact.

teachings.title: The wicked lie in wait to catch the poor
teachings.summary: The wicked, like their father the devil, set nets for the poor and fatherless through vice and scams, and though God's judgment seems delayed He will repay.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 10** acts as a pair to **Psalm 9**, and a meditation on the wicked, against who David is seeking God's judgment.

David opens the Psalm feeling like God's delay in judgment is His hiding Himself, standing afar off, allowing it to continue. We may all feel this way at times. We know God hears us, we have experienced His mercy and blessings and seen His wrath revealed from Heaven, that no man has any excuse to not fear Him...yet, His perfect timing can make us impatient. Even as the saints in Heaven, martyred in tribulation cry out;

**Revelation 6:10**
*And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?*

Obviously, the wrath of God pours out soon after, His vengeance is sure. We can trust it will come. But it is hard for our human minds to wait.

The wicked, through pride, do not seek God. They boast of their wicked desires, and bless those that join in their covetousness. They persecute the poor with their evil devices. Set snares and nets, dig pits, and scheme mischief against the fatherless and the poor. Their iniquity knows no limit.

While their murder and violence is obvious, some of the ways of their deceit is less so.

*He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor: he doth catch the poor, when he draweth him into his net.*

The subtle ways of the wicked, the nets they spread, are not only to blatantly rob the poor of whatever meager wealth they have, but to trap them in temptation.

They are the drug dealers, booze peddlers, pimps and whoremongers, pornographers, bookies running gambling parlors, scam artists with get rich quick schemes...all of the ways, big and small that evil men seek to take advantage of those who are struggling, who have no father to guide them, who are desperate to escape their poverty, who are not strong in faith and so are easily caught up in vice.

The description of these men in verse 9 echos the description of their father, the devil.

**1 Peter 5:8**
*Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.*

These men are as the devil, seeking to take men into their maw, and to bring the righteous to falling, that the adversary can accuse the brethren before God.

David, praying to spur action against these men, reminds God of their pride and arrogant way, dismissing any thought of God making recompense against them. They say that He will not require it, He won't make them pay the wages of their sin. That they mock God, so they deserve swift and immediate recompense.

David often uses these formulas for the Psalms, praising God, reminding Him Who He is, what He's promised, who the enemy are, what the Lord has done against them in the past, what they deserve now, faith in what He will do to them in the future.

Because, God is the judge to the fatherless and defender of the oppressed.

teachings.title: Pharaoh as the example of how reprobation works
teachings.summary: Pharaoh hardened his own heart through the first five plagues before God hardened it, showing that reprobation, like salvation, is a free-will choice in which God gives men over after they repeatedly refuse to acknowledge Him.
teachings.text:
"Oh yeah? What about Pharaoh? God hardened his heart! See he had no free will!"

This is a common argument made by people who lack even basic understanding, have their own ideas and just don't read the Bible and let God teach them doctrine.

In Exodus, we see God through Moses, give Pharaoh multiple chances to acknowledge God and repent, freeing the Hebrews. God sends 10 plagues, and at each we see the pattern:

 Blood: Pharaoh’s heart “became hard” (7:22)

Frogs: Pharaoh “hardened his own heart” (8:15)

Gnats: Pharaoh’s heart “was hard” (8:19)

Flies: “Pharaoh hardened his own heart” (8:32)

Livestock die: Pharaoh’s heart “was hard” (9:7)

Boils: “The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (9:12)

Hail: Pharaoh “hardened his own heart” (9:34)

Locusts: God announces that he has “hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (10:1,10:20)

Darkness: God “hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (10:27)

Death of the firstborn: God “hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (11:10)

It isn't until the 6th opportunity that God gives Pharaoh what he has chosen repeatedly, to not acknowledge God when called to.

As Romans 1 shows:

*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.*

That "*for this cause God gave them up,*"

*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient.*

Reprobate simply means rejected. Unable to come to saving faith having already rejected God, utterly and finally being given up on by God. Pharaoh is an example of how reprobation works. The Bible says they are conscience seared, twice-dead, dogs, sons of the devil, sons of Belial.

Reprobation in the Bible is shown to be as much of a choice as salvation. A Spiritual condition. And it is entirely by free will.

teachings.title: Spiritual blindness is real
teachings.summary: Those who cannot see clear scripture are under a literal God-given blindness, which he learned is real only after giving the gospel and commenting on scripture publicly.
teachings.text:
There will be some who read this channel, see these posts, the clear scripture they are based on, and who will say something like "sure, that's *your* interpretation!" or "Oh yeah, what about this one verse that I have taken out of context?" or "according to a YT video, quoting Wikipedia about the writings of St Autoerotic of Asphyxiation, this means the opposite!"

It is spiritual blindness. It is a supernatural, God-given delusion. They *cannot* receive the word of God.

I used to think that all the verses referring to this blindness we're figurative. That they can't understand scripture because of their own hangups and preconceived notions muddying the waters. That they simply need someone to guide them and to show them their error with the Bible verses that prove them wrong.

It wasn't until I really began giving the Gospel to people, and publicly commenting on scripture, that I came to understand that when God says He blinds them who refuse to see, He means it. It's literal.

teachings.title: To him that hath shall more be given
teachings.summary: God gives understanding freely to those who receive His word, but from hardened hearts by the wayside He eventually takes the light away.
teachings.text:
The lesson of why Jesus uses parables, and the true nature of creation to serve as that parable is given us that we may receive more. That having been given eternal life, and having been made alive in the spirit, we may be given yet more.

It's the opposite of gnosticism, where the secrets are revealed by measures, and final "enlightenment" kept hidden until one archives the ability to see.

The Bible way is that we seeking enlightenment are given it immediately, if we believe God's word. Then our knowledge grows the more we receive it, freely given. The light put on a candlestick, not hidden under a bushel.

It's not hid from those who ask. It's freely given *with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.*

It's up to you if you be stoney ground. It's up to you if you allow thorns to choke you out. It's up to you if you be fertile soil. What you ask for is what you're given, to those that hear.

*For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.*

He that hath not, those without ears to hear, those by the wayside, they are given the chance to receive the word. The seed is sown in their hearts. But even this is taken away eventually. God doesn't shine His light on all men forever. The Spirit tries for a time, but if you don't want to hear the truth, if the seed can't spring up on your hardened heart, compacted like the well-worn soil of the pathway by the wayside, He will take His light away to shine on more fertile hearts. Then it is too late.

teachings.title: Neither will they be persuaded, though one rose
teachings.summary: In the rich man and Lazarus, those who will not hear Moses and the prophets would not believe even if one rose from the dead, as the hardened Jews proved.
teachings.text:
And it came to pass both died, and Lazarus went to Heaven, and the rich man to Hell.

And we are told that the rich man lifted up his eyes to heaven while in torment, and across the great gulf fixed between hell and Heaven saw Lazarus being comforted by father Abraham, and cried out for mercy. To send Lazarus with just a little water, a finger dipped, that his tongue would feel relief from the burning hellfire.

Where in life, Lazarus begged for his crumbs, the rich man is reduced to similar begging.

*But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.*

Daunted, and seeking place for repentance where none can be found, the rich man begs that Lazarus return to the land of the living and preach the truth of salvation to the rich man's brothers that they may be spared this fate.

*Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.*

*And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.*

*And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.*

Jesus makes the point emphatically. They didn't come to salvation by faith, which comes by hearing the word of God. They served Mammon, like the rich man in Hell. And just as they didn't believe Moses and the prophets, they wouldn't be persuaded though a man rose from the dead.

This has a double meaning, where there is the literal example of Lazarus, raised from the dead by Jesus in Bethany, whom the Jews saw come up from the grave after 4 days, made whole by the compassion of Jesus. And of course, Jesus speaks of His own looming death and resurrection. These vipers have hardened their hearts and wouldn't believe even if they saw the son of man rise again.

teachings.title: Pharaoh and the Reprobate Doctrine
teachings.summary: Pharaoh is an Old Testament picture of the Reprobate Doctrine, refusing God's repeated chances until God gave him over and hardened his heart so he could not believe, and modern Christians who reject this truth accept wolves among the sheep.
teachings.text:
*If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God.*

God tells Moses he will be like a god unto Pharaoh, and Aaron his prophet, to be the salvation of His people, freeing them from their burdens and delivering them to the promised land.

This picture of Christ Jesus our Lord and deliverer, John the Baptist His prophet, bringing salvation to the faithful, free from the burdens of sin and death, given to the promised land, the Kingdom of Heaven.

It is a beautiful foreshadowing, done for our edification and as an example that we may know the mind of God.

**1 Corinthians 10**
*Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;*

*2 And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;*

*3 And did all eat the same spiritual meat;*

*4 And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.*

*5 But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.*

*6 Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.*

*7 Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.*

*8 Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.*

*9 Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.*

*10 Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.*

*11 Now all these things happened unto them for examples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.*

**2 Timothy 3:16-17**
*All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.*

The events of the Old Testament are all pictures of those of the New, that we may be thoroughly furnished unto all good works. Just as all of creation exists as a parable, that we may understand the truth of God, without excuse.

Understanding this, and knowing that Moses is a picture of Jesus, the physical deliverance from Egypt by God's mercy, the like picture as a believers spiritual salvation from sin. We are able to draw parallel with the crossing of the Red Sea to baptism, the promised land to Heaven. These foreshadowings are there to edify and guide us. An example.

And so too is Pharaoh. In him we witness the Reprobate Doctrine played out. We see how there are those who, haven been given the chance to know God and be healed, refuse. Who prefer a lie to the truth. Who after attempts to be reached are rejected, and signs and conviction by the Holy Spirit are ignored, God is through with them.

They are given up and given over. For this cause they are given strong delusion. For this cause their conscience is seared. They harden their hearts to God's attempts to extend His mercy and grace to them, and in turn God hardens their hearts that they cannot believe. They are done, being twice-dead. Sons of Belial.

Just as the Israelites will harden their hearts in the wilderness and forget the God that freed them, and so we're denied the promised land. God decides when. He knows the beginning to the end, and knows who will reject him utterly, and STILL sends His prophets to preach, and the wrath of nature to show them, and still they refuse, and so He cuts them off.

The rejection of this Biblical truth has set at odds modern Christians with the judgment of God. Thinking themselves wise, they became fools. They accept wolves among the sheep. Men crept in unawares. Who have the appearance of righteousness but inwards are open graves, full of death.

teachings.title: Pharaoh, Jannes and Jambres
teachings.summary: He teaches that Pharaoh hardening his heart and the magicians Jannes and Jambres picture the reprobate concerning the faith, and warns believers to know such men so their children do not harden their hearts.
teachings.text:
The story of the deliverance of the Israelites from Egypt continues, and the plagues of God increase against Pharaoh and the Egyptians. And still Pharaoh hardens his heart against the truth of the Lord, given to Moses and prophesied by Aaron.

Keeping in mind that this history is a parable of salvation and the spiritual state of man, we have seen the word of God given to man, through His chosen redeemer. A promise of deliverance from bondage and towards the promised land, a paradise of milk and honey, which is given to all who believe. But there are those who refuse to believe. Who harden their hearts, even as the Spirit of the Lord convicts and rebukes them.

Even as *Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses,* the court magicians to Pharaoh, who manage to stage copycat wonders through their sorcery. Tricks. Slight of hand given them by the Devil that Pharaoh would have doubt, refusing to believe Moses. Even they eventually give up, unable to duplicate the wonders of God.

It is fitting that Paul mentions these sorcerers in the context of reprobates concerning the faith. Those who creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins. Ever learning. Never coming to the truth. Like false prophets, these wizards have the appearance of Godliness, His power, sufficient to fool those who aren't saved, who lack discernment. Enough to get others to harden their hearts to the truth of the knowledge of God.

Paul warns Timothy against such people for a reason. God gives us the example of Pharaoh for a reason. As much as the story of Exodus is a picture of salvation in Christ, it covers the entire gambit of human reaction to this gift of grace given us by God.

The believers who praise God when they hear Moses and Aaron tell them of His promise to free them from bondage. The scoffers in the secular leadership of the people. The mixed multitudes, many who aren't of the chosen people, but go along with them.  The Reprobate, like Pharaoh. The unsaved Egyptians who remain behind, in sin. It's all there.

We should heed the warnings and obey the Gospel and understand the nature of man. Be wise as serpents and harmless as lambs. Watch for ravenous wolves who spare not the flock, and bring whole houses to ruin.

Because, if we don't get the full picture, we run the risk of our children falling to the wolves. Turning from the Lord. Hardening their hearts and having the plagues of the book, God's wrath kindled, and turned on them.

teachings.title: Pharaoh a picture of the reprobate
teachings.summary: Pharaoh's hardened heart pictures the reprobate and the Jews who deny Christ and forbid the gospel, who are given over to God's wrath to their destruction.
teachings.text:
The plagues against Egypt continue. We see Pharaoh's heart has been hardened. He cannot believe God's word, even to his own destruction and the destruction of his people.

And even as Moses is a picture of Christ, and the physical salvation of the Israelites from bonds in Egypt are a picture of spiritual salvation from sin and the bonds of the law, Pharaoh is a picture of a reprobate, and the Jews who deny Christ.

Just as Pharaoh refused to allow the children of Israel to go and worship God as He commanded, the Jews persecute Christians, forbidding the Gospel to be preached that they may be saved.

In a like manner, those who call themselves Jews have had their hearts hardened, and also have had the curse of God's wrath upon them, to the uttermost, even when it brings about their destruction.

teachings.title: The Lord doth put a difference
teachings.summary: The final plague shows reprobation is real and final, while the meek in Christ will inherit the earth as Israel spoiled Egypt.
teachings.text:
This is it, the final plague is given to Moses that the wonders of God may be multiplied in Egypt. The Lord will send the angel of death to take the firstborn of every house, even the beasts.

God says "*ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel*." The picture of sin, Egypt, is become death. The picture of Israel, of being God's people, is life and freedom from the burden of sin.

We see in this that reprobation is real, and final. God has taken Pharaoh's hardened heart and made it so he cannot believe the word of God. But Moses found favor in the eyes of the people and those Israelites were given favor in the Egyptians eyes that they should spoil Egypt by taking with them their treasure. Just as the meek, the humble, the believers in Christ will inherit the earth in the millennium, spoiling all nations.

Amen.

teachings.title: Zedekiah hardened his heart
teachings.summary: Like Israel in the wilderness, Zedekiah hardened his heart against God's word and was rejected as reprobate, so believers must not harden their hearts but exhort one another and stay steadfast while the world goes after strong delusion.
teachings.text:
Hebrews 3:8-15
*Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years. Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways. So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.) Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end; While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.*

Zedekiah hardened his heart. Stiffened his neck. He did not do what was right. And God turned against Jerusalem, and fought against her with their enemies. Jeremiah's warnings, the word of God, had no effect on the king.

There are numerous times where we see this play out in scripture. These people who reject the word of God utterly and are fit for destruction. Who are dull of hearing. Blind spiritually. Twice-dead. Dogs.

They are reprobate. Rejected of God.

But we who believe are called to place all our faith in Him, to deliver us. Not to be as the Hebrews in the wilderness provoking God's wrath in Moses time, or the northern kingdom, destroyed utterly by Assyria. Or Judah in Jeremiah's day. To be steadfast and confident in the Lord.

We should be exhorting each other. Edifying the brethren. Hearing God's voice in scripture.

We should not be neglecting His word, chasing after foolish questions and genealogy. Not placing burdens on other's necks. Not putting stumbling blocks before them. But receiving each other in love for the shared joy of the gospel which has saved us, confident in God's ability to deliver us, even as the world goes after strong delusion, condemning itself.

Pray to be like Jeremiah. Called by the chief governor of the temple who had just violently put the prophet in stocks, and yet Jeremiah preaches hard against the king.

teachings.title: Korah's rebellion: unbelief and reprobation
teachings.summary: Korah and the rebels were destroyed and sent to hell for unbelief and rebellion against the man of God, showing God cut off Israelites from His promises.
teachings.text:
*I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not....*

The Lord killed 14, 700 by plague, the households of Korah the Levite (Core in the NT), Dathan and Abiram's households, swallowed up by the earth. And the 250 men offering strange fire before the Tabernacle, burnt up by fire from Heaven.

All for the sin of rebellion against the man of God. And ultimately for determining their way as being correct, despite what God had said.

They sought to take over priestly duties that weren't theirs, to speak out against the man of God. Moses and Aaron, the high priest. And even after God's judgment came down on the 250, The Israelites themselves rose up and were smitten with a plague. God would have wiped them all out there. And as Jude tells us, It was for for unbelief. Because ultimately it's a lack of faith in the things of God that destroyed them.

We see here too that despite the claims of dispensationalists, there was no hesitation by God to cut off those in the congregation of the children of Israel from not only their promises but casting them into hell.

Moses, Who has the power to bind and loose, condemns these men that their sin be not forgiven. So when they die they were going to hell. They were made reprobate by their lack of faith. Apostates. Clouds without water twice dead. And they were plucked up by the roots and cast into the fire.

teachings.title: It was of the Lord to harden their hearts
teachings.summary: God hardened the hearts of the abominable Canaanites so they came against Israel to be destroyed, which he says is reprobation.
teachings.text:
The epic conquest of Canaan by Israel through the power of God, led of Joshua, is an amazing story. One you'd think would be fit for a Hollywood blockbuster.

The taking of the kingdoms, the slaying of kings. The burning of the cities and spoiling of the people to whom God had appointed destruction. Hardening the hearts of those who had committed abominations in the land, that they fed into their own destruction.

*For it was of the Lord to harden their hearts, that they should come against Israel in battle, that he might destroy them utterly, and that they might have no favour, but that he might destroy them, as the Lord commanded Moses*.

This is reprobation. The hardening of men's hearts that they may be destroyed of God.

But Joshua did all that the Lord had commanded Moses. He was obedient and faithful, and the land was delivered unto them. Amen

teachings.title: Philistines who would not repent
teachings.summary: He teaches that the Philistines who felt God's wrath yet asked for His Ark to be taken away picture reprobates who would rather burn in Hell than turn to God, receiving the recompense of Romans 1.
teachings.text:
Going against God can be a real pain in the secret parts. The torment the Philistines received because of their taking of the Ark was brutal. Emerods, or hemorrhoids, ruptured blood vessels and swollen painful boils, consumed the men of every city they brought it to. And deadly destruction throughout.

They move the Ark from their own cities to the Ekronites, who suffer the same. Every place crying up to heaven, saying take this thing away from us.

They have the word of God and see the power of Him revealed in His wrath, the hand of God heavy upon them, but they repent not. They say bring His word away from us.

While it may not be as dramatic in our time, isn't this a picture of what we see all around us? People who are so against hearing the word of God, who despite His wrath upon them for their sin and profanity, their idolatry and false religion, that they would rather be consumed by the fires of Hell for an eternity than to consider turning to Him? Reprobates receiving the recompense for their error which is meet;

**Romans 1:18-32**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: God judges by giving men what they ask
teachings.summary: One of God's sharpest judgments is giving men what they foolishly demand, and no one is saved, chastened or given over without full understanding of the truth and its consequences.
teachings.text:
And so, in **1 Samuel 8**, we see the fruit of unresolved issues that come from allowing corrupt children to be given to rule. And the elders of Israel who should know better, rather than demand the application of the law for Samuel's sons (and likely their own), call for a king. To be as other nations. And set an anointed ruler, who would solve all their problems, rather than deal with them themselves.

This is also a pattern of parents who would rather blow everything up and reject the old paths, rather than simply make the hard choice and return back to the paths of the Lord.

And Samuel prayed to the Lord, seeking Him first. Unlike Eli. While Samuel and Eli both failed as fathers, Samuel sought the Lord and wasn't held as accountable as Eli was, who instead grew fat from his own corruption as he enabled his sons.

And the Lord tells Samuel to listen to the people, that he shouldn't be angry, they haven't rejected him, but the Lord.

*According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, wherewith they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also unto thee.*

One of the most powerful means of dispensing His judgment and punishing people is God giving man what they foolishly ask for, and letting them suffer the consequences of their own decisions.

**Galatians 6:7-8**
*Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.*

The Lord tells Samuel to let them know what having a king over them will result in, so they make their decision with full knowledge and understanding.

He does this as well with all men, His law written in our conscience, provoked by the Spirit, His wrath revealed from Heaven, His mercy revealed in the believer, His word preached to the ends of the earth.

When someone is saved, or disobedient to death, or given up and given over to a reprobate mind to suffer here before eternal torment, it is always with sufficient understanding of the options and tradeoffs, the truth and consequences. Free will is never exercised in ignorance. God's judgment is just, and His mercy great.

And so Samuel tells the people the pitfalls of having a king as other nations do. That a king will take their sons for wars and conquest, their daughters as servants, their wealth as taxes, their inheritance for his servants, their food for his own. Samuel says;

*And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you; and the Lord will not hear you in that day*.

Nevertheless they replied, *Nay; but we will have a king over us*, condemning themselves and the generations for follow with their bad decisions.

And the Lord tells Samuel to do as they asked, make them a king.

teachings.title: When worship becomes a burden
teachings.summary: When a people turn from the true faith even outward worship becomes a burden to them, as with the loss of Sunday blue laws, and God then hardens hearts already hardened.
teachings.text:
Notice that as they waxed worse, they began to see even their superficial and wrong worship of God as an inconvenience to worldly gain. "When will the feast days and the Sabbath be over, we have money to make! Poor people to rob!"

When a people have turned from the true faith, even the most performative forms of false worship become a burden to them. We see that today in America.

We had what they called "Puritanical" Blue Laws, closing up businesses on Sundays and holidays. Allowing people the time to give to God, and to family.

But Catholicism and secularism, and of course, unbelieving Jews, pushed to do away with them until the people saw it as an inconvenience, and demanded everything be open. Liquor stores open for their barbecue and football parties. The mall for their shopping. The poor workers who couldn't afford to not take those hours.

Things were better when families had the time and lack of distractions to file into the pews of the local church on Sunday, and hear the word of God preached.

But now, God is hardening hearts to His word, because the people first hardened them themselves.

*And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord God, that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day*...

Amen

teachings.title: God sends strong delusion
teachings.summary: From Ezekiel 14 and 2 Thessalonians 2 he teaches that God deceives idolaters who will not repent through lying prophets, sending them strong delusion to believe a lie.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 14** opens with elders of Israel coming before the prophet to hear him, but the Lord speaks to Ezekiel, saying that they have idols in their hearts and the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. They have coveted other things before the Lord God. They are unjust and filled with their sins.

And so the Lord says they should be told to repent, and turn from their idols, turn away their faces from abominations. Otherwise, when anyone, Israelites and strangers in the land, seek a prophet, He will set His face against them. And the prophets will lie to them. And the Lord God says He is the means of deceiving them by the words of that prophet. In other words, He will give them strong delusion, that they believe a lie.

**2 Thessalonians 2:11-12**
*And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: that they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness*

The Lord also says that the false prophet will be as punished as these idolatrous men, and all become a proverb and a byword, that Israel turns back towards God.

teachings.title: As a dog returneth to his vomit
teachings.summary: Apostates who taste the truth and fall back, as Peter applies the proverb, are hardened into reprobation and return to their folly like a dog to his vomit.
teachings.text:
The binding of a stone in a sling, trapping it there in its pocket, makes the weapon useless, and so it is equally vain to give honor to a fool.

Sometimes, we try and build up a foolish person by encouraging them when they do right. Unfortunately, this generally puffs them up, and enables their wrongdoing by making them feel justified. The correction of a fool often fails, as we've seen in other passages, how less then their praise?

God, the Creator of all things, Who is blessed forever, amen, rewards the fool, and transgressors. They get what is coming to them, and His rebuke and reproach is far greater than anything we do.

*As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.*

Peter quotes this proverb, and applies it to the false teachers, crept in. The apostates who hear the gospel preached and know the holy commandment to believe, yet fall away back to the rudiments of the world, their later end worse than before.

**2 Peter 2:22**
*But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.*

The apostasy leads to reprobation. As **Hebrews 6** explains, those that have tasted of the truth, and the power of the Spirit, yet reject it, holding the truth in unrighteousness, become hardened. Unable to come to the knowledge of the truth. So they return to their unrighteousness as a dog to their vomit.

teachings.title: Stiff necks and the hated upright
teachings.summary: Those who harden their necks against reproof come to destruction without remedy, and the wicked hate the righteous because they hate Christ and the light that exposes their evil.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 29**, the last of the sayings of Solomon transcribed by order of Hezekiah, begins with the reality of reprobation in those that stiffen their necks to reproof. The Bible often shows examples of heart hardened people, like Pharaoh and the Pharisees, coming to destruction without remedy, despite the reproof of the Lord.

**Romans 1:18-19**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.*

Plagues, curses from Heaven, the reproof of Christ among them, all revealing the iniquity and unrighteousness of men, who refused to acknowledge the truth set before them. And their foolish hearts darkened. There became no more remedy for them, no repentance towards the truth of God. And so they are destroyed.

Vs 2 echos similar sayings, that the rule of the righteous brings joy to the people, but the wicked kings bring mourning.

Vs 3 brings another reminder to honor your father. A wise son will pay tribute to him, but the whoremongers spend what should rightfully be the family's wealth.

Verse 4-8 show some of the ways that a wicked man lays snares for kings and neighbors. With gifts and flattering words, seeking favor. Or by the transgression of an evil man, there lies a snare of sin for others. Vengeance, wrath, or even common cause for filthy lucer's sake, others can be caught up in it when the wicked sin. But the righteous song and rejoice, happily trusting God. Avoiding those pitfalls.

The righteous consider the poor, and turn away wrath. But the wicked don't care. Their scorn for the afflicted and bring others to transgression.

Vs *10 The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.*

The bloodthirsty, the violent man, the scorners and scoffers and fools, they all hate the upright man, the righteous in Christ. Their deeds are wicked, and the good man magnifies the light within him.

**John 3:20**
*For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved*.

Jesus warns us of this truth;

**John 15:18-19**
*If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.*

They hate His children because they hate Him. They hate the light that exposes their evil. They hate reproof and become stiff necked. They hold the truth in unrighteousness.

teachings.title: Blasphemy against the Holy Ghost
teachings.summary: The Pharisees who attributed the Spirit's work to Beelzebub were reprobate beyond forgiveness, and every idle word of the wicked will be judged.
teachings.text:
And as the Jews plot to snare Jesus, He withdraws and heals the multitudes gathered before him, telling them not to speak of it, to the furtherance of the glory of God the Father, and His word;

*Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles. He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets. A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory. And in his name shall the Gentiles trust*

Having cast out a devil that was causing a man to be blind and dumb, healing him, the crowd wondered that such things came from a man, the son of David, heir to his lineage. And again, the Pharisees sought to slander Him, saying Jesus cast out devils in Beelzebub's name.

A house divided against itself cannot stand, and likewise the devil cannot cast himself out and heal. Satan's kingdom then would fall, and isn't that a good thing? But the Pharisees' children went forth claiming to cast out evil spirits in God's name, so Jesus asks, wouldn't their accusations hold against their own? Hypocrites, full of envy and deceit. Blaspheming the Holy Ghost that was upon Christ, claiming the power to heal was from Satan instead.

Jesus teaches that they may slander Him, and be forgiven, but those who falsely accused the Holy Ghost are reprobate. Damned, twice-dead.

*O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.*

As we are judged by our word, and calling upon the name of the Lord, are saved, so to those who speak evil will be judged, and their every word revealed at judgment.

Imagine being in that position, where every evil, dishonest, covetous, snarky, insulting, embarrassing, wrathful, perverse and blasphemous thing we have thought to say is made known to all, before being cast into the lake of fire?

Thank you Lord for my escape in Christ.

teachings.title: Too late, reprobate
teachings.summary: Reprobation is real and comes after God has repeatedly led a man to repentance and been rebuffed, so readers must accept the free gift of salvation now because the Spirit will not pursue them forever.
teachings.text:
I sincerely pray that everyone who comes to the channel today takes the time to read the scriptures I posted here, and study them out for themselves. Comparing scripture with scripture. Proving all things.

In two different epistles, one to Gentiles and the other to Israelites, God inspires Paul in the Spirit to lay out His doctrines that we may know and understand Him. It isn't gnostic revelation, but God reasoning with man that we may be able to go on to perfection, throughly furnished unto all good works. Telling us directly that we may know His will. And in both books, after establishment of the primary doctrines of Christ, we are given the explanation of the reprobate doctrine.

It is also one of the primary doctrines taught in Peter's letters, and Jude. It is the subject of many of Christ's sermons, especially Matthew 23. It is talked about in the OT, and shown us in Exodus as Pharoah goes through the process of hardening his heart until God hardens it forever.

Reprobation is real and it happens after God has repeatedly led one to repentance, only to be rebuffed. There is a point where it is too late, even if that point is death.

If you do not know for sure, today, right now, that you are saved. That you have eternal life. That you have been adopted by God into the promise of His kingdom, please consider His word. Don't wait. Now is the time. Accept that free gift. Repent from your dead works and vain traditions and accept the free gift of salvation paid for by the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

Because the Spirit will not pursue you forever. It can become too late. And reprobates live a hell on earth of misery and filthy affections, until going finally to the Hell that awaits them, to be burned forever. Too late, reprobate.

Don't let this become you.

teachings.title: Impossible to renew them unto repentance
teachings.summary: From Hebrews 6 he teaches that those who were enlightened, tasted the word and were called by the Holy Ghost yet rejected it are reprobate, and it is impossible for them to be renewed again unto repentance.
teachings.text:
Paul in the previous chapters has established his thesis to the Hebrews; laying down the doctrine of Christ and salvation which is the repentance from dead works and faith toward God. The turning from trusting in our own righteousness and towards faith in Christ as the means of our righteousness.

He then further goaded his audience, pricking their ears with scripture they should know, taken from the inspired word of God, *sharper than any twoedged sword,* saying they should be able to handle the meat of the word as they are meant to be teachers to the Gentiles, rather than stuck on the milk of the word, these basics, like babes. And so he begins building upon this foundation to delve deeper into the Spirit-inspired truths of God.

He writes God willing, they can leave behind *the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment,* the milk so to speak, and get into more complex teaching. Because, to be more perfect, (which in the Bible means complete, not without flaw as we take it to mean today), we need to grow in His word and in understanding.
