 He stresses this with good reason. If they are saved by faith, and so by definition understand those basics of faith as their confidence for eternal life, then why keep going over them?

Who is "*ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth*?" Reprobates.

And in the following verses, Paul in the Spirit, writes again of those rejected and cursed by God.

*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

It's vain to continue addressing those who should have the knowledge of the truth with these basics, unless they be reprobate.

It's impossible for them who:
- have been enlightened to the truth; *Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them*
- That have tasted the gift of salvation, not accepting it but having understanding of it; *when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations*
- Who are *made partakers of the Holy Ghost,* who as Jesus said, calls all men to the truth, *when He is come, He will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment*
- Who *have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,* again "tasted," they sampled it, they heard the word preached, they saw the revelation of God in nature, law written in their hearts, felt the Spirit which is the conscience that convicts us as He reproves the world of sin...

It is IMPOSSIBLE for these people to be renewed again unto repentance. They can't believe. Their foolish heart was darkened. Hardened. Their conscience seared as with a hot iron. They are twice-dead, plucked up by the roots to be burned.

The window to accept the gift of Christ has closed, as mentioned in the previous chapters. Everyone has a chance at receiving the free gift of grace, *While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.*

Now is the hour of salvation.

But those who withstand the call, the rebuke of the Spirit, who knowingly changed the truth of God into a lie, it is impossible for them to come to repentance. They are cut off. Rejected.

*They crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

**Matthew 27:22-25**
*Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified. And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.*

teachings.title: Churches that no longer teach reprobation
teachings.summary: He charges that most churches no longer teach reprobation and wrongly say it is never too late for sodomites and corrupters of the word, though scripture says their end is to be burned.
teachings.text:
The majority of churches out there, the apostate churches teaching the damnable heresy of works salvation especially, the Lordshipers and fruit inspectors, but even many Biblical fundamentalist churches with the right understanding of the plan of salvation, many of these no longer teach reprobation, a doctrine that was common from the beginning of the church as we see in NT scripture, and was common even within my lifetime.

They teach that those showing the outward signs of reprobation, specifically the sodomites but even others, who put themselves forth as teachers of God's word while taking from it or adding to it, knowingly making the truth of God into a lie, these congregations will say there is still a chance for them. That it's never too late. That it is possible to bring them again to repentance, despite the Bible being very clear their final end is to be burned. *Rejected and nigh unto cursing.* Twice-dead. Dogs.

And by failing to teach the meat of the word, as it offends some and is too hard for them to chew and swallow, they stay in the milk of the word, going over the doctrine of Christ again and again.

teachings.title: A Fearful Thing to Fall into God's Hands
teachings.summary: Those who taste the truth and turn back to the old covenant have no sacrifice left for sins, only a fearful expectation of judgment.
teachings.text:
So if that is the practical application of our faith, and the understanding of our salvation in Christ, the end of sacrifices for sin, boldly going before God, serving Him and assembling together, then what is the implication for those who instead turn aside the faith and the new covenant to return to the yoke of the old?

*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

*He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.*

*It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.*

Again, this is a warning to those who may have tasted the truth but are withdrawing themselves, influenced by the Judaizers who were afflicting believers with the doctrine of dead works.

That if there is no reconciliation by animal sacrifice, if there never has been, and you have this knowledge of the truth in Christ but turn away back to the Old Testament, rejecting the New, you remain under the wrath of God. You have the guilt and fear of judgment upon you. Worse, the knowledge of the truth adds to that burden of guilt, how much worse God's vengeance is on those who should know better? And by the end of this epistle there can be no doubt. If they fall away from faith in Christ and refuse to repent towards God after hearing this preached, well, it's a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

teachings.title: Our bad report and hardened hearts
teachings.summary: Hebrews warns that saved believers who fall back into dead works can give the lost cause to harden their hearts until it is too late, so Christians bear a grave responsibility to walk righteously so that any rejection is the unbeliever's own fault.
teachings.text:
One of the key points throughout the book of Hebrews is that if we who are saved fall back again to the old ways, to the sin offerings and dead works, to bitterness at reproach, to neglecting our Christian walk, we bring others down with us, who have not received salvation. Who haven't yet come to the saving faith. Who may be pricked by the Spirit and hear the power of God's Word, and so taste of the heavenly calling and fall short by our example. And *thereby many be defiled.*

Especially knowing that there comes a point where their rejection of the truth and refusal to find faith in the hope we have can leave them reprobate. Either in death, or by being turned over to a reprobate mind by God. We give them cause to harden their hearts. To be dull of hearing. To not believe our report.

Our faith alone cannot bring another to the knowledge of the truth. But our lack of faith can lead the lame to stumble, as we bring them to uneven paths, leaning on our own understanding.

Many of us harp on the Reprobate Doctrine because it is an extremely important Biblical truth that far too many are ignorant of, or reject to lean on their own understanding or follow the wisdom of men. There is a point where it is too late for some. And once they are given up and given over, they are twice-dead. Children of Hell, fit for burning.

But this isn't simply for the cursing of those who have been rejected by way of their hardened heart, but a grave warning to those of us who have been blessed by the faith in God's promise and redeemed in the blood of Christ.

Faith comes by hearing the word of God.

So does reprobation. The Bible says they have the knowledge of the truth but don't wish to retain God in their knowledge. That they turn the truth of God into a lie.

If they will harden their hearts and turn away from the truth, don't let it be that we, like David, *despised the commandment of the LORD,* and give *great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme.*

Don't let it be by our bad report.

Rather, if they reject the truth of God and His offer of grace and mercy, let it be because by our righteous conversation. Our behavior. That they see our faith and that we walk the straight paths, and if it offends them so be it. If our separation from the things of this world and the peace we have because of the blessed hope we've attained offends them, then it's their own dull hearing and seared conscience to blame.

This is a great responsibility.

teachings.title: It is too late for some
teachings.summary: Contrary to the claim that God never gives up on anyone, Scripture shows many individuals and nations from Sodom and Pharaoh to Belshazzar and Judah for whom it became too late, and though most have until death to believe, some are given up while still alive.
teachings.text:
*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts...For this cause God gave them up to vile affections...*

"God never gives up on us!" That's a lie. "It's never too late to repent and believe!" That's not what the Bible says.

As longsuffering as God is, He is clear in His word that it is too late for some. The angels of the first habitation that fell in their pride. The people before the flood. The people of Sodom and Gomorrah. Pharaoh and the Egyptians. The people of Canaan who had committed abominations. The Edomites to whom God promised a land to, but they eventually were given up and destroyed. The wicked kings and queens who killed the prophets of God. Israel, the northern kingdom, the 10 tribes therein, bred out of existence and scattered. The Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes whom Jesus condemns in their own unbelief. Judah, destroyed for the unregenerate Jews who rejected the truth of Christ Jesus.

*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, And in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation*.

In the book of Daniel, Babylonian Kong Belshazzar saw the writing on the wall. Literally. Judgement of God against him had been declared by the Spirit writing upon the wall of his feast hall. It was too late for him. That night Babylon fell to the Persians and Belshazzar was slain.

Over and over again we see God reveal the truth to people, and call them to repentance. Sometimes, like the Gentile city of Nineveh, they listen and are spared His judgment. God repents of the evil He would do to them as recompense for their error.

Others, like Pharaoh, harden their hearts until it is too late.

In the end times, as the day of the Lord approaches, the Bible tells us that there will be people in denial, believing their own vain imaginations, right up to the end.

**1 Thessalonians 5:1-3**
*But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

And like the day of the Lord, only God knows the day or hour where He will give up people to their own destruction.

It is a blessing of His mercy and grace, the longsuffering of the Lord, that for most people the final nail in their coffin is their natural passing to death and hell. They have the chance to change their hearts and accept the free gift of salvation right to the end of their lives. But not all people.

Some refuse the truth so utterly God gives them up that they may feel His wrath by their own unnatural lusts consuming them.

teachings.title: No plan B for the cut off
teachings.summary: From Romans 11 he teaches that those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate, and that doubting this by imagining a secret plan to win them back questions the judgment of God.
teachings.text:
And so, *As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes.*

God would that they believe and be saved. He would glory in the older being brought back into the Kingdom with the younger. But it can only happen through faith, and those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate.

*For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

It's all about faith. We are all in sin and grace is offered all of us.

*O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!*

Many find it unfair that some are cut off, they refuse to believe the Reprobate Doctrine, they doubt the judgment of God. They think He must have some secret plan to win them back. A plan B. But the only plan is Christ. And Him crucified. And it is not for us to question the judgment and mercy of God. He will have mercy on whom He has mercy. It's not up to us to tell Him, but to humbly submit to His will.

*For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: The peace offering and the reprobate doctrine
teachings.summary: Leviticus 19's ban on eating the peace offering on the third day pictures the reprobate doctrine of Romans 1 and Hebrews 6, that there comes a time when it is too late to receive God's offer.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 19** contains what is essentially a restatement of the 10 Commandments, and the practical separation of the children of Israel from the heathen that were in the land, both Egypt and Canaan, to be holy as He is holy.

I am the Lord your God and am holy. Fear, or respect/honor you father and mother. Keep the sabbaths. Turn not unto idols or make molten gods, we can see it is the same spirit as the law given to Moses at Saini.

The Lord says that all sacrifices are free will offerings, or they don't count. This is consistently stated, and it carries over to believing on the Lord Jesus Christ, as every sacrifice is a picture of Him.

The injunction against waiting three days to eat of the peace offering, least it be abominable, to me, is a warning against waiting to accept the Gospel.

*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

Reprobation, as we learned in **Romans 1**, comes when the truth of God is given but not received. As **Hebrews 6** stresses, if one tastes of the heavenly gifts and falls away, it becomes impossible to renew them again unto repentance.

There becomes a time when the peace offering goes from bringing peace and reconciliation, and becomes an abomination and not accepted.

Everyone who does this shall bear their iniquities. They have profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord. Their soul shall be cut off.

This is the reprobate doctrine in the Old Testament. It is a consistent doctrine, taught throughout scripture. It can be denied by modern Christians who falsely teach that it is never too late, despite the clear meaning of scripture that tells us that it can be.

teachings.title: God gives many chances, then judgment
teachings.summary: God warns nations, backsliders and the lost again and again, but after rote religion and wickedness continue, His judgment comes and He forbids intercession.
teachings.text:
The preaching of the word of God continues, Jeremiah prophesying in the Spirit that God is casting His judgment upon a wicked and perverse generation of Judah.

As He frequently does, the Lord, being long-suffering and full of mercy and grace, extends His hand first. Saying; *Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.*

Because the judgment of nations is done on this earth. And the wickedness of those who are His people will be met with the rod of correction and reproof.

We serve the living God and as His sons, the spiritual seed of Abraham, we too face this judgment for our inequity and the inequity of the people.

But, because of His love, grace is always available to those sons who repent. The prodigal who returns home. The nation where the people who call themselves by His name turn back towards Him, God promises to heal.

God instructs Jeremiah to preach at the door of the temple, to those in Judah entering in for sacrifice and burnt offerings, but who outside the temple blaspheme God. Serving other gods. Commiting wickedness; they
*steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not*, and yet out of habit and vain faith they return to His temple to do the performative religious acts, that do not save them.

*Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord.*

This is the scripture Jesus preaches during His scourging of the moneychangers in the Temple;

**Matthew 21:13**
*And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.*

It's the same spirit that gripped the Pharisses, rote practices of ordinances but nothing given to the weightier matters of the law;

**Matthew 23:23**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone*

God says He has spoken to them, warning them, calling out to repent and they didn't hear. *They answered not.*

When God says this, He obviously means it literally, that through the prophets He has instructed His people and warned them, but more; He had recently allowed the entire Northern Kingdom, and the 10 tribes therein, to be destroyed and scattered by the Assyrians, for just such behavior. The whole seed of Ephraim, being the most prominent tribe of Israel, represents those northern 10 tribes. He reminds them "I have cast out all of thy brethren."

God gives His people chances. Repeatedly. He gives unsaved people multiple chances as well. The Spirit moving to rebuke the world that they may come to believe. But eventually, be it judgment upon a nation that is destroyed, judgment against a backslidden believer where they are rebuked and eventually called home if they don't respond, or to the unbelievers who don't wish to retain God in their knowledge, and are made reprobate. God gives us multiple chances and warnings to repent towards Him and His mercies.

God says to Jeremiah, don't even bother praying for intercession. He is done with these people. This is on them, their last chance.

teachings.title: God's patience runs out
teachings.summary: Men and nations who reject God's word and only cry out in calamity find that His longsuffering has an end, and even the backslidden saved can be chastened or taken home.
teachings.text:
In **Jeremiah 37**, we see the king and his princes, those in power besieged by Babylon. They had not harkened to the Lord and did not listen to the wisdom of the word of God, preached by the prophet Jeremiah. But in their calamity they sought him to pray for their salvation from the Chaldean horde.

In a like manner, many men will wait until the foxhole is being shelled to ask God for deliverance. To protect their lives. Even as they reject His word, and salvation of their souls. They shout out "Oh my God!" with no faith. They want to eat their cake and have it too.

But God again and again tells us that He calls early, and often. That wisdom is crying out her voice in the streets.

That, as a mother hen, the Lord seeks to gather us as she would chicks under her wing, but they would not listen. And they slew the prophets and did what they wanted, and so when destruction is due, God laughs at their calamity.

Salvation, be it the individual soul liberty of those justified in Christ, or the physical salvation of a nation, is not extended indefinitely. God is longsuffering. He is mercy and His grace abounds. But He is clear. There comes a time for both people and nations, where His patience runs out and He scourges with a rod of iron. His wrath is kindled. Too late, reprobate.

This has application in the saved Christian's life as well. He wants to form us into vessels fit for His use, that we may bring forth fruit after our kind. But if we resist Him and live for ourselves not heeding His word, separating ourselves to the Gospel, becoming backslidden, being reproached again and again and ignoring it, God will eventually destroy you. Punishment will be more severe for us than the wicked who prosper. Or taking us home earlier than maybe we would have been.

At some point it is too late, even for the saved.

teachings.title: Denying the reprobate doctrine endangers the flock
teachings.summary: From Judges 19 he warns that churches that deny the reprobate doctrine and teach it is never too late let sodomites and predators in among the flock, then cover it up out of pride.
teachings.text:
It is worth pointing out that the Levite and his party were closer to a city of the Jebusites, but not wishing to lodge for the night in the city of a stranger, he sought the city of Gibeah, thinking they would be safer among Israelites, to be among Benjamin.

Very often Christians will be disarmed in their judgment by blindly trusting people at church. People professing to be fellow Christians. People who claim to have repented of their evil ways, who have a good story for a testimony, about turning from the most wicked sins to be saved.

Christians may even turn from dealing with an unsaved neighbor, to seek out the services of a "brother."

But God has given us fair warning. Their very countenance gives them away. Churches that harbor sodomites are like Benjamin did, allowing the wicked to creep in unawares, are endangering their flock.

It starts with denying the Reprobate Doctrine. Teaching that all men are able to be saved at any time, that it's never too late to repent.

But the idea that hearts are hardened, ears made dull, eyes blinded to the truth, that some are past the point of feeling, conscience seared as with a hot iron, given up and given over to a reprobate mind, that is, rejected of God, is taught throughout scripture.

In the NT, Paul, Peter and Jude write extensively on the subject. The preaching of Christ in the Gospels affirms it.

And after denying reprobation as real, congregations will begin to drift towards "repent of your sins" heresy. They may give lip service to "grace alone, faith alone," but they will sow the seeds for a works-based false gospel in the minds of the people. This leads to a certain prideful view, where the worse the sinner who "repents," the more powerful the testimony seems in their eyes. "Look who we helped turn around to Christ. Aren't we good?"

And so you have youth pastors and music directors who molest children or rape teen girls. Men who should have taken Christ's advice and drowned themselves in the sea, rather than offend little ones.

And the pastors and deacons who allowed these monsters in will do whatever they can to cover it up. In their pride, like the men of Benjamin, they would rather go down fighting to defend their poor judgement than do what's right, and admit they were wrong.

They will lie and claim it is to keep the testimony of Jesus Christ from being slandered, to defend the gospel from scoffers, but it is selfish and wicked.

And even good pastors, godly men who are saved by the right gospel, who have won hundreds to the Lord, can fall prey to their own pride and embarrassment at their lapse of judgement. And when it comes out, the damage done is far worse than had they done the right thing.

*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: The bitter end of an apostate
teachings.summary: Amaziah, who knew God's things but turned to idols, shows the apostate whom Hebrews 6 says cannot be renewed to repentance and whose destruction is greater.
teachings.text:
The reign of Amaziah, son of Joash, King of Judah, lasted 29 years. With a heart towards God in the first, and obeying the word of God given by the prophet, in the end he turned towards other gods and would not harken to the word of the Lord.

When he set to go to war against Edom, he hired men from Ephraim, of the northern kingdom to bolster his ranks. When the prophet of the Lord came and told him he would not prosper with them, that God would ensure his loss, Amaziah sent the men away. But only after being assured the money he had paid for their hire would be restored to him by God.

They left, angrily, and spoiling Judah on their way.

Amaziah wins the battle at Mt Seir, defeating the Edomites, but slaughters his captives and takes their idols and set them up to be worshipped in Jerusalem. Wicked. And from there, the puffed up king sought to ally with wicked Israel, and was instead humiliated by their King Joash, both in word and battle.

He refused council with the prophet of God, threatening to have him slain.

Instead, he eventually is chased into hiding and slain, because he had turned from the Lord.

The bitter end of an apostate, someone who has an understanding intellectually of the things of God, even tasting of the gifts, but in the end rejecting Him. Their destruction is greater than those who simply never sought the truth.

**Hebrews 6:4-8**
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned*.

teachings.title: Wisdom crieth, and God will laugh at their calamity
teachings.summary: Wisdom calls men to repentance as God did through the prophets and Christ, but those who hate knowledge are given over, and God will not answer but laugh when their calamity comes.
teachings.text:
Continuing **Proverbs 1**, we see a warning against joining in another man's sin. Not being led to robbery and violence by greed. That ultimately, it ends in their own blood and death. Crime doesn't pay.

Next, Solomon tells us of Wisdom, as a woman, though this is more the feminine of the word than a gendered being, and Wisdom is much like the Spirit of God, today.

The original Hebrew word for wisdom, *hokhmah*, is a feminine noun, and Solomon will compare the virtuous woman of Wisdom to the harlot, the "strange woman," the folly of fools later in the book.

But the literary device aside, like the male Spirit of God, He reproves and reproaches, and calls men to truth. Like God has done through the inspired word of the prophets, crying out, how long, ye simple ones? Scorners and fools reproofed.

Wisdom is "poured out" in spirit. Calling us to repentance. God's words, the wisdom itself, made known unto us. As God promises to write the law in our inward parts.

This echos so many passages, especially when Jesus rebukes the Jews;

**Matthew 23:37** *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

**Isaiah 65:2** *I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts*

Those thoughts are foolishness. They set at naught His counsel. This crooked generation refused to accept His Wisdom, and so, He will laugh at their calamity. He will mock the. When their fear cometh.

What a sobering thing to be mocked of the Lord. To get to the place where you've been given up and given over. When you are destroyed in His presence, cast into eternal torment, and God will laugh, because He gave you ample warning. The wrath of God being revealed from Heaven, that you had no excuse. But they didn't wish to retain God in their knowledge.

*Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord*

But those who fear the Lord, and receive wisdom from Him, have a better promise;

*But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil*

teachings.title: Remaining in the congregation of the dead
teachings.summary: Those who see the way of truth but reject it without truly believing are given over by God to a reprobate mind and cannot be brought again to repentance.
teachings.text:
*The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.*

**1 John 2:19**
*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.*

**Hebrews 6:4-8** 
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

**John 6:64-65**
*But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him.*

**Proverbs 21:16** is another proof text for the understanding of the reprobate doctrine. The knowledge that a man who wandered out of the way of understanding remains in the congregation of the dead.

Notice it isn't that the person HAS understanding. They are not perfect in their ways. They saw the path, maybe followed it for a while, and left it. They tasted of the Spirit, but rejected it without ingesting, without being indwelled. They never fully believe. And when they reject the truth of God? God gives them up and gives them over. It is impossible for them to come to the knowledge of the truth. To be brought again to repentance.

**Romans 1:21-22**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools*

These people knew the truth, but did not glorify Him. They knew the gift, but weren't thankful for it. Their foolish heart was darkened. Hardened. They were waxed fat, dull of hearing. Eyes that could not see.

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts...Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections...And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient*.

They are given over to Satan. Reprobate concerning the faith. Clouds without water, twice-dead, branches cut off for unfruitfulness, cast into the fire. Conscience seared.

They remain in the congregation of the dead.

teachings.title: Normal unsaved sinners are not reprobates
teachings.summary: Ordinary unsaved sinners still have a conscience and God's law in their hearts and have not been turned over, whereas reprobates are twice-dead children of Satan, neither alive in the flesh nor in the Spirit.
teachings.text:
It's important to recognize that normal unsaved sinners are not reprobates. They haven't been turned over by God. They commit normal sin, common to man, but occasionally have righteous actions and are repulsed by the unnatural lusts of the reprobate, having still a conscience and the law of God written in their hearts.

Sons of perdition, sons of Baal, of their father the devil, are spiritually twice-dead as the saved are born again.

The normal unsaved person are spiritually Ishmael. First born of the flesh, born of water  They aren't heirs of the kingdom, aren't sons of God, aren't receiving the blessing, etc, where as the second born (or born again by the Spirit) are Isaac, and so heirs to the promise. The Bible calls the unsaved (such as we were), children of wrath and children of disobedience.

Reprobates are not alive in the flesh or in the Spirit, being twice-dead. Plucked up by the roots and cast into the fire. These are the children of Satan.

teachings.title: Soul winning creates reprobates
teachings.summary: He teaches that preaching the Gospel, as God intends, also creates reprobates, because the truth must be known and rejected for men to be given up as Romans 1:21-25 describes.
teachings.text:
One aspect of spreading the Gospel that most miss, and misunderstand, is that as many receive it, even more reject it, and in doing so, eventually run the risk of reprobation. Soul winning can and does create reprobates, and that is intended by God. Every hearing is a seed sown, or watered, and could be what leads to harvest. But the same message of truth is really required for the reprobate to know and reject to lead them to that state.

**Romans 1**

*21 Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.*

*22 Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,*

*23 And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

*24 Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:*

*25 Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: Reprobation is not about the sin
teachings.summary: Whether a person is saved or given over to reprobation depends on his relationship with God rather than the size of his sins, and most people are ordinary unregenerate sinners for whom there is hope until death unless they become reprobate.
teachings.text:
This is why you may have a 40yo murderer, a serial fornicator, an adulterous person, a drunkard or whatever, who, overcome with guilt and coming to the realization of what awaits them, accepts the Gospel sincerely, and you may have a 14yo who has hardly left the house, let alone committed grave sin, who willfully blasphemes the Holy Spirit and rejects God utterly, and is given over to reprobation.

It's not about the sin but your relationship with God.

Most people fall in neither the camp of the saints or the reprobate, they are just unregenerate sinners, with all too common lusts of the flesh. There is hope for them until they die, least they become reprobate.

teachings.title: What reprobation is
teachings.summary: He defines reprobation as a free will condition of unbelief in which men who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge are given over by Him, made unable to believe and twice-dead, with unnatural lusts as its effect rather than its cause.
teachings.text:
Reprobation is a condition caused by belief, and not wishing to retain God in their knowledge, to no longer be bothered by conscience, unwilling to believe and so being given over, given up by God and made unable to. They are given what they want, and made twice-dead.

It is a free will choice as much as salvation, and isn't determined by level or severity of sin.

The sins a reprobate mind may invent runs to those sins not common to man, unnatural lusts.

Reprobate isn't a synonym with depravity or degeneracy. It is the **cause** of such behavior.

teachings.title: Blasphemy of the Holy Ghost and reprobation
teachings.summary: From Mark 3 he teaches that blasphemy of the Holy Ghost leads to reprobation, that some like the Pharisees, Cain and Pharaoh are turned over to a reprobate mind and unable to believe, and that unnatural sin is a symptom of reprobation, not its cause.
teachings.text:
**Mark 3** sets the same pattern we've seen in the other Gospels, of Jesus healing or teaching and the Jews who oppose God trying to use the occasion to be rid of Him. Here, Christ heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath. As we have just read in **Mark 2**, Jesus continues to make this point, that it is lawful to do good on a sabbath. That Sabbaths were made for men, not men for the Sabbath. He is the Sabbath.

Failing to lay hands on Him, Jesus makes His way to the sea, and multitudes came to see Him from all about the region, so much so He asks a boat be ready to help Him depart, should the crowd be too much. He heals the multitudes, and gains more who flock to see the wonders, and glory God, and some unto believing on Him as the son of God by faith. This is important, as He reprimands the unclean spirits He casts out to silence their proclamation that Jesus is Christ, the Son of God.

We see that then, after retreating to the sea, Jesus then goes to the mountains, continuing to preach to the masses following Him. He formally ordains the 12 Apostles to preach and heal in His stead, so as to minister to the crowds that have gathered.

And because people from all over Galilee, Judea, and beyond have come to see Him, and the proximity of Nazareth to Capernaum, where much of Christ's ministry had been, His family, mother and half-brothers and friends He grew up become concerned, not knowing who Jesus truly is. They thought Him crazy. But the scribes accused Him of being from Satan, and the Holy Ghost by which He cast out these demons, they label an unclean spirit. A blasphemy He warns is unforgivable, and is a way to reprobation and damnation.

As Jesus says a house divided cannot stand, as if Satan turned on his own. How can Satan cast out Satan?

And all sins of men will be forgiven. This is important. A penitent believer will be forgiven all manner of sins, but the blasphemy of the Holy Ghost and deliberately changing God's word (Rev 22).

These are direct causes of reprobation that most Christians will accept. The will also concede death without believing is final, and damned. But they often struggle with the idea that some, not wishing to retain God in their knowledge are turned over by Him to a reprobate mind. A rejected mind. Hearts hardened. Conscience seared. Twice-dead. **Unable** to come to the knowledge of the truth. This is the case for many of these Pharisees and scribes. Such was the case for many in the Old Testament, Cain and Pharoah for example. It continues to be the case today.

And because people confuse reprobation, a spiritual state of man, finally rejected of God, and the unnatural lusts and sins committed by reprobates, they argue, that if all sins be forgiven, then there is no such thing as "too late, reprobate." This puts the sodomite cart before the horse.

Unnatural sin is not the cause of reprobation, but a symptom that it's occured. It is important to get that right. It's never about the sin itself, but the state of a man's heart towards God. Belief unto salvation. Unbelief and vain beliefs of the unsaved which can be overcome with the word and repented of unto faith, or rejection of belief to the point God gives up, stops shining the light. The Spirit no longer calls. Three states one may be in, two final before physical death, one final at that death.

teachings.title: The Reprobate Doctrine and the three states of man
teachings.summary: The Reprobate Doctrine, taught throughout both Testaments, describes one of man's three spiritual states, the twice-dead who are utterly rejected by God, and Christians must stop lumping them in with common sinners so they can defend their families and communities.
teachings.text:
The Bible gives us many doctrines that we should observe and put into practice. From the nature of God, our creation, to the Gospel of reconciliation and redemption, and how it all will end, to how to live our lives, handle our marriage, raise our children, run a church, and a nation. Both spiritual things and best practices for our carnal lives.

But one of the most important doctrines, which touches on both the spiritual nature of man and a warning to heed here on earth, is the Reprobate Doctrine.

The teaching on reprobation is one of the most overlooked but relevant doctrines in the Bible. It is taught throughout both Old and New Testament, which not only gives description of how one becomes a reprobate, but example after example of those that do, and warning after warning of how to handle them, the evil they do, and the signs to watch for to identify them.

Reparation, the final and utter rejection by God of those who have finally and utterly rejected His overtures of grace, the call to Christ and the prodding and patience of the Holy Ghost, is one of the three spiritual states of man.

There are the unregenerate sinners, dead in spirit but with the conscience of God within, who, until death, could hear the call and believe on Jesus Christ and be saved. They are the children of disobedience.

Those who call upon the name of the Lord, believing God's testimony and, spirit quickened. They are saved, born again believers. Called the sons of God.

And there are the reprobate. Twice-dead. Conscience seared. Dogs. Sodomites and worse. Filled with all unrighteousness. Hearts hardened, ears dulled. Unable to come to the knowledge of the truth. Rejected of God. Turned over. Given up. Clouds without water. Vipers. Deserving death. Unmerciful and implacable. The sons of Belial. The children of the devil.

Often Christians, who seeking to be kind and show mercy, thinking they are doing the right thing, will completely ignore the final group, lumping them in with the common sinner. Holding out hope, even when they reveal their wickedness in ways exactly as God's word tells us they will.

It is this lack of understanding, as well-intentioned as it's meant to be, that causes so much trouble and trauma in this world today. People who engage in uncommon sin and unnatural lusts, who blaspheme the Holy Ghost, who deny Christ, and lead others to damnation by getting them to deny Christ as well.

I've covered the scriptures dealing with reprobation dozens of times in this channel. The clearest teaching on it is in Romans 1, but the Epistles of Peter and Jude talk about it, hebrews, Jesus himself speaking of the Pharisees and the other unbelieving Jews, and found in Psalms and in the stories of Sodom and gomorrah, and the pharaoh of Egypt... Through the prophets who are killed by these reprobates, and in the Book of Revelation where it tells us of most of humanity reprobating themselves to take the mark of the beast.

We know and understand who these people are because God has given us the information and understanding if we seek it.

I encourage all of you to study on the reprobate Doctrine and come to an understanding to better defend yourself, your family and your community from these people.

teachings.title: For this cause God gave them up
teachings.summary: Romans 1 explains the cause and effect plainly: because men rejected God, He gave them up and over to a reprobate mind, filled with all unrighteousness, not some.
teachings.text:
For... Because that... Because that...Wherefore....For this cause...God gave them up...God gave them over to a reprobate mind....Being filled with **all** unrighteousness. Not some. All. For these reasons, here listed, because that, they become this. All unrighteousness.

It's fully explained in clear terms if you've an ear to hear.

teachings.title: The wrath of God revealed from heaven
teachings.summary: God reveals His wrath through creation and conscience so all are without excuse, and those who hold the truth in unrighteousness and worship the creature have their hearts darkened.
teachings.text:
So, in our prior instalment we see the righteousness of God is revealed to man through those that are saved sharing the Gospel of God in Christ Jesus with others. Here we see that God also reveals His nature, His wrath, from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men.

Their literal unrighteousness is part of His wrath. Man is punished by their own sin. We see it all the time, that the consequences of sin is a curse, teaching the wages of sin is death. Nature has revealed to us this truth, the system of consequence. We see it in the downfall of our own current society. We see the effects of sin in our own lives.

Because that which may be known of God is manifest in those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. God has shown men His judgment.

Man has a conscience. The law of God is written in our hearts. The Spirit has come to convict men of sin that they may know they need salvation. The law worked in the OT times to do the same, as a schoolmaster to our unrighteousness that we may seek salvation in the Lord.

These invisible things of God are visible, clearly seen, from the creation of the world through now. And His wrath is understood by His creation. Man understands right from wrong, as Paul gets into later in Romans.

We see His power and destruction in nature. We see it in the flood. In Sodom and Gomorrah. The judgment of nations.

We see the eternal power of the Godhead and so, all men are without excuse.

But men that knew God through His revelation, weren't thankful to God and didn't glorify Him as God, but became vain in their imaginations. Men knowing the judgment and wrath of God made up stories to explain it. Devised often complex systems of works and worship of idols to justify their sin. Vain, meaning unprofitable and a waste of time. Even today they invent a false god out of the Biblical God, and their perverse version of Jesus, while ignoring the truth of His judgment.

These people, the Bible says, have their foolish hearts darkened. Hardened. They become worse with time, clinging to their vain beliefs and not recognizing the truth of God through His revelations to us.

Prophets. His word. His power. The Gospel. His wrath. These things are given that all men seeking truth shall find it.

But those who became vain in their imaginations, whose foolish hearts are darkened, who profess themselves wise become fools, and change the glory of an uncorruptible God into idols, images made like unto corruptible man, like the Catholic church or the Orthodox that split off it. Or like unto birds, and animals and creeping things. Worship of nature. Worship of themselves even.

Worship of the created more than the Creator.

Because of all that...well, Paul tells us what ends up happening to these people in the following verses.

teachings.title: Wherefore God gave them up
teachings.summary: He traces the Romans 1 progression in which men who turn God's truth into a lie are given up to uncleanness and vile affections, so that sodomites are punished by their own lusts and no longer convicted.
teachings.text:
And so, we rewind slightly to yesterday's verses to see the because that/wherefore/for this cause - logical progression of what follows those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. Who knowing God, Who is revealed to us in multiple ways, who knowing His judgment and His wrath, and knowing His righteousness, believe a lie and deny His power.

Because when they knew God through revelation, but didn't glorify Him, but rather their imaginations, their foolish heart, which is darkened. And they worship the creature more than the Creator. Idols. Nature. Rocks. Fables. Traditions of men.

**Wherefore God gave them up** to uncleanness. Because of their rejection of the truth for a lie, God let's their lust dishonor their own bodies. The curse of being left to their own lusts is used by God to punish them. The same as we see His wrath through the consequences of sin and repent, they are blind to it and so He gives them up to wallow in their lusts and receive the wages of their sin.

Continuing the same thought, Paul writes; *For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections*. For which cause? They turned the truth of God unto a lie. What vile affections? *Women did change the natural use into that which is against nature. And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned with lust one towards another.*

So we understand the process, God reveals His truth. Some refuse to see it, and not only refuse (as most people who never believe), but worse, they turn the truth into a lie. And are given up to their lusts, which brings them to God allowing their vile affections to take hold of them. He gives up. The Spirit isn't convicting them of sin, in fact their own delusions justify it in their darkened hearts.

And this is clearly talking about sodomites and lesbians, and transvestites for that matter. Leaving the natural use, to go against nature.

Why? That they receive *recompense in* themselves *their error which was meet*. That they suffer in their flesh, in their lives the wages of sin. That they are cursed by God to fulfill their own lust, and so be punished by the consequence of it. The recompense that was meet, meaning appropriate to, commiserate to the error. They get punished with being queers so they can suffer for it.

Because the wrath of God is a revelation to all men to lead them to repentance towards God in Christ, and because they reject that and turn that truth into a lie, and deny God His glory, and are unthankful in their vain imaginations, God gives them up to their own vile, unclean, not-normal, lusts that they burn with.

They don't "struggle with sin," they are consumed by their own lust. God gives them up to it so they can suffer the fullness of His wrath. It's no longer a lesson to bring them to conviction that they may be saved. God has given them up to this.

teachings.title: Why the reprobate doctrine matters
teachings.summary: He argues that the reprobate doctrine, taught fully in Romans 1, ranks just behind salvation and wrath in importance because it explains the third spiritual state of man, Jews, psychopaths and why tolerating sodomites destroys a society.
teachings.text:
Some Christians question why some of us make a big deal about the Reprobate Doctrine. They say that it's an incidental doctrine, or they deny it outright (having no other consistent and Biblical interpretation that works, given all the clear scripture that supports it).

But, as Paul lays out in Romans, it falls just behind the truth of God, Jesus, salvation and wrath in importance. Romans is a comprehensive theological breakdown of Christianity. The implications and understanding of salvation in Christ, and we are given it just after the Gospels and Acts for a reason, and reprobation is explained fully in the first chapter of it, again for a reason.

That reprobates are the focus of the epistles of Peter and Jude, as well as Hebrews and other Pauline epistles should also be noted as the importance God gives it, as a way of recognizing and understanding just who they are, what they do and how they become that way.

It explains their behavior and why their choices are made but it also gives us incentive to spread the truth and live in a way that reveals the righteousness of God, that maybe some will get it before "it's too late, reprobate!" Before they die perishing or are given up to their own foolish and darkened heart.

It is as important (and tangentially related) as the JQ, and the Biblical understanding of Jews in relationship to Christ, that they are antichrists.

Understanding Reprobate Doctrine as it is biblically taught explains Jews, why they are what they are.

It answers questions so many have regarding psychopaths, mass murderers, pedophiles, why tolerance of sodomites destroys a society, how the judgment of God works on those who aren't saved, here on this earth, in the flesh.

Most people understand perishing, death and Hell.

Few people understand salvation and eternal life.

Even fewer understand the third spiritual state of man, reprobation.

And it is from this ignorance of scripture that the Devil tempts us. It is by getting people to listen to their own conceits and the logic of man, rather than scripture that Satan traps us in snares, leads us to sin and in our ignorance, sow tares among the wheat.

We will finish off chapter 1 tomorrow, and then continue through Romans, giving it the proper study it deserves.

teachings.title: Cause and effect in Romans 1
teachings.summary: Romans 1's because and for this cause show that sodomy is the effect of reprobation, not an unpardonable sin, and that reprobation is a process in which God gives chances first, as with Cain and Pharaoh.
teachings.text:
Again, going back a few verses to keep the context, we see Paul describe the cause and effect, that **because** and **for this cause**, **wherefore**, **and even**... conditional phrases that inform the following consequence.

Many people who aren't familiar with the Reprobate Doctrine confuse effect with cause. They believe what's being taught is that queers can't be saved because sodomy is an unpardonable sin like blasphemy of the Holy Ghost or taking the mark of the beast.

But when we read **Romans 1,** and study biblical reprobates like Cain and Pharaoh, we see there's a process, that God gives them chances to make it right.

**Genesis 4:4-8**
*And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him. And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.*

God gave Cain a chance. God is longsuffering and patient. But Cain took his chance and instead slew his brother, and became rejected of God.

teachings.title: Waters of life shut up from reprobates
teachings.summary: Hezekiah stopping the fountains against blaspheming Sennacherib pictures how those who do not retain God in their knowledge have the water of life shut up from them and so come to spoil and harm God's people.
teachings.text:
Here in **2 Chronicles 32**, and we have the last chronicles of the King, Hezekiah. Sennacherib, a captain of Assyria has come to lay siege against Judah and her walled cities having already begun its conquest of Israel.

Knowing the hosts of the enemy are going to surround Jerusalem, compassing it about, Hezekiah has his men stop the flow of water to the fountains without the city.

He has done great public works projects, and throughout his reign in Chronicles, we see how his diligently seeking the Lord has blessed him with civil engineering marvels (later we see he turned a river to bring water closer to the city).

So his order to shut up the fountains so that *Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?*

When Sennacherib comes, he immediately begins to profane and blaspheme God.

The parallel I see to the Reprobate Doctrine, that those who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge and blaspheme and speak of the Lord God of all creation as if he were like other gods, weak and ineffectual and not to be trusted or relied on, have the waters of Life shut up from them.

While all others are told by Jesus to come and drink freely, reprobates come to spoil that which is God's and to do harm to his people, because they have been denied partaking in the water of Life.

teachings.title: There is a generation always with us
teachings.summary: The wicked generation of Proverbs 30 is not one age group but the reprobates always among us, who despise parents and are pure in their own eyes (Romans 1).
teachings.text:
**v11-14** contains an indictment of a group of people, a crooked and perverse generation;

*There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother. There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their filthiness. There is a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up. There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men*.

Many are always quick to apply this to "kids today," or to Baby Boomers, and arguments can be made to support this, but it's a mistake to isolate this as purely prophetic of specific cohorts united only by age, and attribute to them all these evils.

The generation is always with us. There IS a generation like this, the Bible says. There are always evil people, who curse their father and do not bless their mother. Who reject the instruction of their parents and do not honor them. Disobedient to parents.

There are always segments of the population who are pure in their own eyes, justifying the filth of their flesh and the lust in their hearts.

There are always prideful and arrogant people, who see themselves as above the righteous, while they live in the gutter. Who reject the ways of the Lord, to walk the paths of folly.

People who use words as weapons, inventors of evil, who use and exploitation and extortion, usury and inequity to destroy others.

There are always reprobates among us.

**Romans 1:29-32** 
*Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: the unbelieving Jews rejected
teachings.summary: He teaches that Paul frames Jewish persecution as reprobate versus elect, that per Jeremiah 6:30 the unbelieving Jews are rejected of God while saved Greek and Jew are now His elect, and that Jewish antichrists are turned over to a reprobate mind.
teachings.text:
Paul is again writing of the reprobate, the rejected of God, and those abominable and disobedient deceivers going after the *elect*, or chosen.

When Paul frequently writes of the Jewish persecution of the faithful, he frames it in terms of the reprobate vs the elect, because he is trying to show the Gentiles that THEY are the chosen people of God now, and the Jews the rejected:

"*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them."* **Jeremiah 6:30**

This deliberate use is misinterpreted by calvanists who miss the point being made; that Saved Christians, "Greek and Jew" are now God's chosen, His elect, not the unbelieving Jew. And that they in their jealousy and envy, have further become filled with all unrighteousness.

To be a Jew of the flesh after the coming of Christ is to reject God. To not retain Him in their knowledge. Jews whole identity is that rejection, and God's reprobation of them in return.

This is why Jewish antichrists are so wicked. They are turned over to a reprobate mind.

teachings.title: Romans 11 and the reprobate nation of Israel
teachings.summary: Paul's argument in Romans 11 is that the remnant are those Jews who believe the Gospel, and that God does not hold out salvation indefinitely but cuts off the unbelieving, whether individuals or a nation, and turns them over to reprobation.
teachings.text:
Here in Romans 11, Paul is finishing the JQ begun in chapter 9 and 10, as it pertains to Israel after the flesh, the nation, now that Christ had come.

This builds on the theme he has from the start; that all men are without excuse in condemnation, and further some men and nations condemn themselves by bringing God to reject them utterly, unto reprobation. That even with the law, the Jews were condemned and without it, so were the Gentiles. That the Gospel of faith alone in grace alone of the resurrection, into His kingdom, was the promise that faith was placed in. Without works. *To him that worketh not.* That this election of grace applies to the Gentile as much as the Jew. That there is no difference between Jew and the Greek, that if all are condemned, then all are saved in Jesus if they believe. It's flawless doctrine, relentlessly building on itself.

Here in Romans 11 Paul is finishing the thought of what to say about the physical Israel, the Jews, given all this doctrine. What does the Gospel of Christ mean pertaining to the old covenant? (God is a logical God, who wants us to *reason together* with Him)

Dispensationalism rests primarily on vs 1-5, and, like most bad doctrine, isolating verses out of context to achieve it. They say "see, God's not done with Israel!"

But here Paul specifically is offering himself as the example, that the remnant is those who believe the Gospel. For we know from the prior chapters that there is a conditional state to salvation, belief. Obeying the Gospel. And so any Jew who believes will be that remnant. Same as the Greek who are grafted in to the promise by their faith.

Verse 6 has God hammer again the point that salvation is not by works. It is 100% by faith, least it no more be of grace. Because it is a gift and the rewards for work is a debt owed. (Works-nibbas BTHO, again)

So, having established that the Jews after the flesh have to believe, Paul circles back to Romans 1 and reprobate doctrine, calling in mind the imprecatory prayer of David to blind the wicked who reject the truth of God, unto damnation.

However, Paul prays that the Gentiles receiving the blessing and promises, being grafted in, provoked his kinsmen to repentance. That they turn from stubborn unbelief to accepting the Gospel. That they who are believe would be sent, preaching the word, and by hearing, physical Israel believe and be grafted in again. That by his own example living for Christ he gets his nation to want to emulate him and be saved.

This plea is a familiar lament to many Christians. We all have unsaved relatives, often close. Friends, coworkers. People for whom we earnestly pray accept the free gift of salvation but who have hardened their hearts.

Paul's example of being worthy of emulation is a model for us, that we live the Gospel in a way that draws them to the light and softens their hearts that they may be willing to believe.

The warning to Gentiles against becoming arrogant regarding their position relative to grace and the reprobate silver nation of Jews should also be taken to heart.

A Godly nation can easily turn from the truth and be burned in the fire, just as easily as recalcitrant Israel could have a revival in Christ and be graft back in. Prodigals restored as heirs.

Dispies falsely make this an unconditional statement rather than an argument; that Jews **will** be graft in regardless of their own belief or wickedness.

Paul has built his case, in the Spirit, that everything here is contingent on believing God's law and promises, whom all men know, and knowing are condemned without excuse, except they believe in the gospel, which is of faith in Christ's crucifixion and resurrection for the remission of all sins, that this is a gift available to everyone, without works, entirely of grace, but that God doesn't hold it out to be taken indefinitely, and that at some point He will cut off the unbelieving, reject and turn them over to reprobation. Individual salvation to eternal life, or a physical nation on earth, it's the same.

teachings.title: The wicked husbandmen given over
teachings.summary: In the parable of the vineyard Jesus shows the Jews who knew the truth yet sought to kill Him, so God gave them over to a reprobate mind and will destroy them and give the kingdom to others, contrary to dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
Following the story of the fig tree which Jesus cursed for not producing fruit, He tells a parable. The master leaving a vineyard to be tended sends for the gathering, and the husbandmen he'd entrusted with the land beat and kill his messengers. He sends his only begotten son and they plot to kill him and take the inheritance for themselves.

With this not so thinly veiled analogy, Jesus puts the Jews who are seeking to kill Him on notice. They discern that Jesus is talking about them. Unlike most of His parables that fell on deaf ears. The Bible says "*they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way*."

It is amazing to us who believe that there are those who knowing the truth, seek to silence it, even with the Son of the Lord standing there in their presence. Even with the history of the Jews, who killed the prophets of God, and now plot to do the same to Christ.

They wish to not retain the word of God and the truth of Christ in their knowledge. They sought instead to take the inheritance of an earthly kingdom for themselves by His death. They worship the creation more than the creator. And God turned them over, gave them up, to a reprobate mind to do those things which are inconvenient.

*Reprobate silver men shall call them.*

Again, the dispensationalist idea that the Jews held a special place and God wasn't through with them yet, is a lie. They were given the advantage of the oracles of God and the ministry of Jesus Christ in the flesh, and rather than repent towards God, they sought to destroy Him.

And like the master of the vineyard, *he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.*

It does not say He will take it from them for a time. He destroys them and gives the Kingdom to those who will produce fruit, giving God the increase, in His Son's name.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: a national identity
teachings.summary: Quoting Romans 1:18-32 and Jeremiah 6:30, he teaches that the Jews who rejected the Messiah are reprobate by their individual free will and collectively judged, so that it is their national identity.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18-32**

*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,*
*And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:*
*Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

*For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.*
*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

Speaking specifically of the Jews who would reject the coming Messiah;

**Jeremiah 6:30**

*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

It is their national identity. By their individual free will. Collectively judged.

teachings.title: God judges nations; Jewish identity is rejecting Christ
teachings.summary: God is no respecter of persons in offering salvation but judges nations collectively, and the Jews' identity rests on rejecting Christ, so they are given over as in Romans 1.
teachings.text:
God is not a respecter of persons, the Bible says repeatedly. He does not care if you are great or small, rich or poor. Man or woman, Greek or Jew, where you're from or who your parents are. He gives us all the same offer of salvation and adoption in Christ. As individuals we have free will.

God does judge nations. He does favor some over others at times, and destroys many who go too far astray. He curses the land stained by blood of violence. Sodomy. Fornication. Of people, collectively, to the fourth generation.

We are to know the judgment of God and emulate it. Not being a respecter of persons, giving the Gospel to whomever we meet, but judging ungodly nations for what they are. Including our own.

Every nation carries that burden, where the godly among them must turn towards God so that He may heal their land. Not just ours.

Jews, from the most Orthodox to the most liberal Reformed to the atheists, all draw their identity not of blood, (none can tell you their tribe or origin), not of true ethnicity. They draw their identity directly from rejecting Christ Jesus as the Messiah, and having not the Son, have not the Father. Being liars who are antichrists. Being reprobate IS their identity.

No other nation or ethnicity is founded on this lie and pride in rejecting God.

And because they don't wish to retain God in their knowledge, *He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.*

And so, Romans 1 applies to them as it applies to all that go the way of the Pharoah.

teachings.title: Modern Jews as reprobate silver
teachings.summary: Modern Jews are not the descendants of the twelve tribes but a people defined by rejecting Jesus, given up and cursed by God as reprobate silver, which undoes the dispensationalist hope for their salvation.
teachings.text:
Before getting back into the chapter itself, I want to reiterate that whatever else they are, Modern Jews are not the sons of Judah from the Old Testament.

Whether they are Edomites or Khazarians, or some other people, regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story and Jewish fables, We know they are not the descendants of the 12 tribes of Israel. To the extent they may have some of Abraham's blood in them, So does most of the world.

The one defining characteristic of all modern Jews, and by modern I mean going back to the first few centuries AD, or the foundation of Judaism 400 years after Christ, all Jews hold as their primary identity the rejection of Jesus. Be they Ashkenazi, Arabic, Turkish, Polish, Reformed, orthodox, atheist, conservative or liberal... Every single Jew is an antichrist. And God will make of them a synagogue of Satan.

Reprobate silver will men call them. For they have been given up and rejected by God.

I make this caveat because as we know, dispensationalism is about modern Jews, not the 12 tribes of Israel which no longer exist and haven't existed since 70 AD.

When they say that they think that God isn't finished with the Jews or that all the Jews will end up being saved at the second coming of Christ, they are talking about this reprobate group that the Bible says aren't actually Jews. They aren't even Israel after the flesh let alone spiritual Israel, which are all believers.

And God has cursed them.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Judah rejected
teachings.summary: From Jeremiah 6 he teaches that Judah, with its false prophets crying peace, was rejected of God as reprobate silver, and that God judges nations the same way today, especially those called by His name.
teachings.text:
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace....Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

Jeremiah, in the Spirit, is preaching hard against Judah, which has become totally corrupt, and faces judgment from the North, by the invading armies of Babylon which God is warning He will allow to conquer and spoil them.

And the prophets and priests are telling the people "Peace. Peace" when there is no peace. They speak soothing words, withholding judgement, leaving the people with a false sense of security. That everything is fine.

That their sacrifices and their expensive, imported incense, the performative religious acts they do, will offset the Idolatry, fornication and wickedness.

Jeremiah preaches that this is not acceptable to the Lord and they will be spoiled and left desolate. Reprobate, rejected by God.

A millennium after God takes the children out of Israel, clearing the land of the nations that committed  abominations, driving then out before them, and here they sit facing the same judgment. The northern kingdom of 10 tribes, wiped out and dispersed by the Assyrians, and Judah about to be overrun by Babylonians. And despite the warnings of the prophet, none of them repent of their ways. They break the covenant and despite God's longsuffering, His wrath is upon them.

How can we not help but see the parallels and understand we face the same judgment?

God judges nations by their works, and especially by those who call themselves by His name. If those claiming Him, who say they are Israel, fall away, He is going to cut them off.

It is a real 🎯 you are here-moment.

teachings.title: Idolatry and reprobate nations
teachings.summary: Nations that turn to idolatry behave as Romans 1 describes and are given over to God's judgment, as the Canaanites and Israel were, and Catholic and Orthodox idolatry has brought that same judgment on Europe and America.
teachings.text:
*Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the Lord your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the Lord thy God hath forbidden thee. For the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When thou shalt beget children, and children's children, and ye shall have remained long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, and shall do evil in the sight of the Lord thy God, to provoke him to anger: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed. And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.*

This prohibition against Idolatry was not only to Israel. The nations being driven out before them had fallen to Idolatry, forgotten the Lord God that brought them out of Noah and his sons. They committed abominations. They behaved as **Romans 1**:18-**25** describes; reprobate.

*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

Moses tells them that they will suffer the same judgment as a nation if they turn to idols. That they will be destroyed, made desolate, driven from their homeland, scattered. This is God's judgment on all nations that turn from Him to serve idols, and even moreso those nations claiming to be called His.

This same judgment that destroyed the Canaanites, ultimately destroyed the Israelites, who were rejected of God. Reprobate silver. Given up and given over to their vain imaginations. And this same judgment exists today.

Roman Catholicism and Orthodoxy especially, have turned entire nations to idolatry, and in doing so, brought the judgment of God upon them. This is why Europe was overrun with Muslims in the past, and why it is happening again today. And in other Christian nations that have allowed altars to idols to flourish are seeing the same judgment, especially America.

More than Sodomites, more than antichrist Jews, people claiming to be Christian yet bowing and praying to idols, worshiping the created more than the Creator, are the reason for our current state.

We are overrun with the fruits of a Reprobate mind; sodomy and abominations. We are being ethnically cleansed. Our children barren and filled with all unrighteousness. And it first starts with idolatry. This is the primary lesson of the Reprobate Doctrine.

teachings.title: Make no peace with reprobates
teachings.summary: He teaches that the Canaanites were reprobate nations God commanded destroyed, and that believers today should mark and avoid known reprobates, keep them from their congregations and urge magistrates to execute God's law.
teachings.text:
