I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

**Joshua 24:15**
*And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.*

Forcing people to make this choice is the purpose of revival. It is the fruit of preaching the word and going out to win souls. It forces people to choose.

Some will hear the word and be converted unto eternal life. But many will reject Christ and decide to harden their hearts and hold the truth in unrighteousness.

The revival led by King Josiah was shortlived. When he died in battle, his sons were made king, first Jehoahaz, who was then carried away to Egypt, and then Eliakim aka Jehoiakim. Both did evil in the sight of the Lord. In our study of **Jeremiah**, we covered these kings and the wickedness of Judah in their day, when Babylon came and made Jerusalem a desolation, fulfilling the word of God. They did evil in the sight of the Lord and willfully and knowingly turned to the sins of their fathers and the abominations that they did.

The Lord giving Judah one last chance to know the truth, to have it read to them by Josiah, and acted upon by his hand, meant that while many believed unto righteousness, most chose death.

So that when God's wrath came upon them, they were without excuse.

Soul-winning is what we are called to do, but the more we do it, the more the gospel is proclaimed to every creature, and gone out to all the world, the more people will become reprobate. Even our own families.

At some point, the fullness of the Gentiles will come in. Everyone who will be saved will be, and the rest will choose to worship the beast and take his mark, and condemn themselves.

Our job is to go work the harvest. To force the issue. To make people decide if they choose life or death.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord while he may be found
teachings.summary: God is longsuffering, but there comes a point when He withdraws Himself from a nation or an individual and they become reprobate, so men must seek Him now while He may be found.
teachings.text:
The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation.

Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them?

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them*.

God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked.

This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found.

**Isaiah 55:6-7**
*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

**Matthew 13:14-15**
*And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.*

teachings.title: Before it is too late, reprobate
teachings.summary: The false idea that it is never too late to be saved has led many to Hell, since men who put off grace harden their hearts like Pharaoh, so seek peace in Christ while you can.
teachings.text:
The false idea that it is never too late with God for people to get right and get saved, that as long as you live, there's always a chance for salvation, has led so many to Hell. They put off to tomorrow the gift of grace. They stay in the pleasures of sin for a season, rather than esteeming the reproach of Christ, or having respect for the recompense of the reward.

But rather, like Pharaoh, they harden their hearts and stiffen their necks and dull their hearing. They seek after vain jangling and smooth preaching, and those telling them "peace and safety" when there is no peace.

Like Israel, they chase after idols and put their faith in horses and chariots, turning towards Egypt spiritually. Or worse, pitching their tents towards Sodom.

God's wrath comes like a thief in the night, His judgment is righteous and true. Wake to Him and seek peace in Christ while you can.

Before it is "too late, Reprobate!"

teachings.title: Children and the base rule a judged nation
teachings.summary: Child rulers, dishonoured elders and promoted sodomites are not causes of coming judgment but signs that a nation is already under God's judgment.
teachings.text:
The prophet Isaiah continues his preaching against Judah, and the judgment of the Lord that is already upon them.

The Lord has taken from them the stay, or that is the stores of food and water. There is famine and drought.

Further there is a lack of leadership in the land, a lack of righteous judges and men of honor. A lack of prophets and wise elders. In their place are children. And because of this, the children rise up against their elders, and dishonor their fathers, and promote the base, that is the morally wicked. The perverts and sodomites.

No one reputable wants to lead, because the nation is ruined and fallen.

These are signs of a nation already under judgment. We often mistake these things as a reason we will eventually be judged, but the Lord is clear they are the results of already being judged.

*The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.*

I believe this is the expression and affectations that sodomites and other reprobates all seem to have. That weak mouth and wide, whites of their eyes showing. The lispy voice. The cruel smirk. The proud look of those who have rewarded themselves for evil.

But the Lord wants His children to know they will be blessed, even in the collapse around them, that the righteous will eat of the fruit of their doings. And the wicked shall receive their reward.

But the people of the nation are led by children and women, and being brought to error and sin. The shame of a nation, which no longer has righteous men to rule over them, having had them taken away in judgment.

teachings.title: Compromisers and the old paths
teachings.summary: Those who call standards legalism repeat Israel's compromise, and God eventually gives such people up to their delusions.
teachings.text:
With all the talk about "legalism" and preaching against standards, and calling "the old paths" divisive, you have to wonder if the compromisers actually read chapters like Ezekiel 20.

The children of Israel continually left His statutes, and His judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them - old paths that He gave them, that they might know that He is the Lord that sanctified them.

They compromised. They said to themselves "Why offer at the temple? We have high places. We can give our sweet savor to this idol in His name. We can keep our own sabbaths, not His." And so each generation filled themselves up with the measure of their fathers, and rejected more and more the path of the Lord.

The people compromising today, claiming to be doing the will of God by telling people to not worry about keeping the law, that it be well with them. To not have moral standards and behavior. They are a stubborn and rebellious people.

And you'll note that God eventually will give them up to their own delusions. To allow them to go on down the road to perdition. If they don't hear His voice and see the value in His statutes, then He eventually will leave them to wallow in that mire. To return to their vomit. And the firey flames will consume them.

teachings.title: The scorner seeketh wisdom and findeth it not
teachings.summary: Those who hate God are given over and never find wisdom, so the wise keep silent under accusation as Christ did and flee foolish teachers rather than sifting knowledge from them.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Proverbs 14**, we are given several wise sayings, often repeating the points to really drive them home. Archetypes of wisdom contrasted with the folly of fools and warnings against liars.

The wise builder, embodied especially in the "wise woman" of verse 1 who "*buildeth her house*," representing constructive, diligent wisdom that strengthens family, home, and community, where the foolish woman destroys her home, as plucking a hen. Bit by bit.

Again, we are told the upright fear the Lord. This healthy respect for God is the source and substance of wisdom. But those on the crooked ways of the perverse hat the Lord.

They have been made to know the truth, by the wrath of God revealed from Heaven against the ungodly, but they hate Him and truth.

**Romans 1:28**
*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient*

God will give the wicked what they desire, and by rejecting them utterly, give them over to their perverse ways to their own destruction.

The fool speaks out because of pride, but the wise keeps their lips quiet when insulted. This is a hard one for many, including myself. Hard to remain quiet when being falsely accused and raised on or our pride is attacked. But Jesus showed us the way;

**Matthew 27:11-14** 
*And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest. And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee? And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.*

Humility in the face of accusations is often the most potent defense. Counterintuitive but like much of God's wisdom, it goes against man's understanding.

*Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox.*

There are tradeoffs in life, and we are better for it. Sometimes, to get things done you have to be willing to shovel the dung. Another example of delaying gratification to your betterment.

Faithful witnesses do not lie, but a false witness will. It seems obvious, and repeated in verse 25: *A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.* When given the opportunity, we should remember the deliverance we received, and speak truth to deliver others. This is pleasing to God and foundational in the 10 Commandments. Thou shall not bear false witness.

*A scorner seeketh wisdom and findeth it not...* reminds me of the false teacher, a reprobate who Paul describes in **2 Timothy 3:7** *Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.*

How can they, without the fear of God? How can they when they scoff at truth and hold it in unrighteousness? When they hate God rather than fear Him?

So we should reject the foolish man when you perceive he does not have knowledge. Again, flee a false prophet or someone claiming to know who just spouts nonsense. They ultimately will lie and speak falsehoods and defend their pride. They make a mock of sin, joking about evil ways. Flee these people. Don't take company with them, and don't try to sift any knowledge from them. They may be right about something, but in the end it isn't worth the rest that comes with it.

*The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.*

No one but you and God can know the heartache or the joy you feel in your heart. Truly know it. And you can't know another's, even when you empathize or rejoice with them. It's an important thing to keep in mind when others deal with you, or you're dealing with others. Have grace because of this limitation, and thank God for it, too. If our heart were open to men, it could be embarrassing and shameful. Thank God we don't actually wear our hearts on our sleeve.
